title: Audit B: silent no-op detector — empty manual bodies vs original size, plus a NOOP annotation gate
description:
src/game has ~1039 single-line '{}' method bodies (counted 2026-07-03). Some are faithfully empty in the original; an unknown number are silent placeholders that compile, run, and do nothing — the worst gap class because nothing fails loudly (exactly how TViewMgr::UiRuntimeSlot110/F8 hid: no FUNCTION marker, so invisible to reccmp scoring AND invisible as stubs).

Detector (new check in tools/workflow/, wired into 'just ui-gap-report' and optionally 'just gates'): parse manual sources for method definitions with empty (or trivial '(void)arg;'-only) bodies; resolve each to an original address via (a) its // FUNCTION/SYNTHETIC marker if present, else (b) the header's slot comment (the '// 0xNN 0xADDR' convention in TView.h etc.), else (c) symbols.csv name match; then compare against symbols.csv size. Flag: EMPTY-BUT-BIG (original > ~16 bytes = not a real no-op — port it), EMPTY-UNMARKED (no marker at all — invisible to reccmp; either add the marker or delete the phantom method), EMPTY-VERIFIED (original is genuinely a ret/ret-imm stub).

Annotation convention to make the audit converge (one-time cleanup, then a decomplint-style gate): every intentionally-empty body must carry either a // FUNCTION marker (so reccmp scores it 100 against a real empty original) or an explicit '// NOOP: verified empty in original 0xADDR' comment. New unannotated empty bodies then fail the gate, so this gap class can never silently regrow. Follow the existing gate pattern (tools/workflow/check_marker_hygiene.py, wired via just gates); keep the gate baseline-tracked initially (like antipattern-gate) so the existing 1039 don't block commits before triage.

Also sweep the sibling shape: '(void)args; return nullptr/0;' placeholder bodies in manual files outside src/autogen (the factory placeholders are known; find the unknown ones).

Acceptance: detector output triaged — every EMPTY-BUT-BIG either gets a port issue or is disproven; EMPTY-UNMARKED count driven to 0 (marker added or method removed); gate lands baseline-tracked and passes on main.

title: Audit A: vtable-slot coverage matrix for the UI subtree, ranked by runtime reachability
description:
Build tools/reccmp/ui_gap_report.py (+ 'just ui-gap-report' target) producing a per-class, per-slot coverage matrix for every class with a // VTABLE annotation (404 today), prioritized to the UI subtree (TEventHandler descendants, CWnd/CMcWindow family) and the manager singletons (TViewMgr 0x66f120 69 slots, TDisplayMgr, TAssetMgr, TMacViewMgr, TSimMgr, TMultiplayerMgr, TTurnEventDialogFactoryRegistry).

Per slot, join: (1) original target address from the vendored Ghidra DB vtable dump (just ghidra-vtable-dump / the vtable_extent.py approach), resolving ILT thunks to real targets via docs/ilt_target_map.csv; (2) ownership from config/function_ownership.csv — manual file vs src/autogen/stubs partN (=stub) ; (3) original byte size from symbols.csv col 4; (4) reccmp score via tools/reccmp/compare_batch.py single-JSON-parse mode; (5) declared-but-empty status (cross-ref with Audit B). Classify each slot: PORTED(score), SHORT-PORT (ported but recomp size < ~60% of original — the RunRegisteredDialogFactoriesByEventCode 0x491cc0 class of bug), STUB, EMPTY-UNVERIFIED, MISSING (no owner at all).

Ranking (this is the systemic part): weight each gap by runtime reachability, not size alone — (a) class is instantiated in ported code ('new T(' grep over src/game + recovered_globals.csv singletons) => its stub/empty slots are live silent no-ops or null-call risks (the EIP=0 crash class from 1uj.57.1); (b) slot is called from at least one ported function (xrefs from manual-owned callers, global-xref-oracle style); (c) original size. Emit top-N as a 'these methods silently do nothing at runtime today' list.

Validation cases the report MUST catch to be considered working: TViewMgr slots 0xF8/0x110 (empty bodies, real originals — bd imperialism-decomp-key); TGameScorePicture::HandleEvent 0x57b620 (empty body, 219-byte... [sic] real original); the 15 factory placeholders in turn_event_dialog_factory.cpp.

Reuse before building: tools/workflow/check_* scanners show the source-scanning idiom; tools/reccmp/core_impact_ranking.py may already contain the reachability-weighting skeleton — check it first. Output: build/ui_gap_report/*.csv + a markdown summary; do not hand-edit generated files.

Acceptance: report runs from a clean checkout ('just ui-gap-report'), catches all three validation cases, and its top-20 list is triaged into port issues (or explicit verified-noop annotations).

title: Systemic UI-gap audit: enumerate every unported handler, controller method, and callback in the UI system
description:
Complement to the phase-by-phase bring-up roadmap (imperialism-decomp-1uj.57): instead of discovering blockers one crash at a time, build repeatable audits that enumerate ALL gaps in the UI dispatch fabric up front. Motivation from the 2026-07-03 session: three UI blockers were each found by expensive ad-hoc tracing, yet all three belong to mechanically-detectable classes: (1) TViewMgr::UiRuntimeSlot110/F8 are silent empty {} bodies with no FUNCTION marker while the original bodies are real (class: unverified-empty-body); (2) RunRegisteredDialogFactoriesByEventCode dropped the packet-attach tail vs the original listing (class: short-port, recomp size much smaller than original size); (3) FUN_00484230 movie-done callback has zero code xrefs because it is only referenced as a data pointer (class: unowned registered callback).

Raw materials all exist: config/symbols.csv (address|name|symbol|SIZE|type|prototype), config/function_ownership.csv (address -> manual file vs src/autogen/stubs), reccmp batch scores (tools/reccmp/compare_batch.py, one JSON parse for ~9600 fns), 404 // VTABLE annotations + just ghidra-vtable-dump, the vendored Ghidra DB via pyghidra (xrefs_to, raw_disasm), and the rtti-oracle's 471 CRuntimeClass descriptors. The audit = joins over these + a few new scans, emitted as one 'just ui-gap-report' target with CSV/markdown output, re-runnable after every merge.

Children: (A) vtable-slot coverage matrix ranked by runtime reachability; (B) silent no-op detector (empty bodies vs original size) + NOOP annotation gate; (C) MFC message-map audit (every WM_/custom-message handler's port status); (D) data-section function-pointer scan (registered callbacks, dispatch tables); (E) turn-event-code coverage matrix (screen-by-screen completion map). Counts as of 2026-07-03: ~1039 single-line {} bodies in src/game, 2450 autogen stub functions, 15 factory placeholders.

Tooling pitfalls to inherit (documented in memories/tools): jpype bulk Memory.getBytes silently returns zeroed buffers — use Java-side Memory.findBytes or per-byte getByte (see tools/ghidra/raw_disasm.py header comment); Ghidra decompiler output is degenerate on the turn-event factory cluster — parse listings/jump tables, not decompiles; ILT thunks (0x401000-0x409ab5) must be resolved to their targets before any join (docs/ilt_target_map.csv); name_paired_no_marker ownership rows are real owners despite lacking markers (sync-ownership prune trap).

Acceptance: 'just ui-gap-report' runs end-to-end and each child audit has produced its ranked gap list; top findings converted into concrete port issues feeding 1uj.57 phases.

title: Port the main-menu screen factory case: event 0x5dc in InitializeGameSetupScreenControlsAndModeTags (0x4538a0)
description:

Use the established widget-block recipe (heuristics note 33; worked examples: BuildTurnEventDialogResources_2508 at 0x44a810 and ForEvent898 at 0x45d520, both ported in commit 2b1eee48, plus shared helpers RegisterUiResourceEntry/SetUiResourceStateFlags/SetUiResourceLayoutValues/BindUiResourceTextAndStyle in ui_resource_pool.cpp). Per-code TViewMgr hook for 0x5dc is UiRuntimeSlotF8 (empty body, TViewMgr.cpp:1331 — port with imperialism-decomp-key or here).

Depends on: the packet-attach fix (factory trees must join the paintable tree) and the advance-chain issue (something must dispatch 0x5dc). Related: imperialism-decomp-1uj.51 (this is one of its 17 giants — coordinate, don't duplicate).

Acceptance: DispatchTurnEventSlot4C(0x5dc) renders the menu background + buttons in the main frame; factory scores >0 and gates pass.

title: RunRegisteredDialogFactoriesByEventCode drops the packet attach + anchor reposition (0x491cc0)
description:
Verified against the original listing 2026-07-03 (just ghidra-listing 0x491cc0, 129 bytes): after the factory loop finds a non-null result (EDI), the original does TWO things our port (src/game/TTurnEventDialogFactoryRegistry.cpp:77) silently drops:

1. if (pEventPacket != 0) pEventPacket->AttachChildControl(result, 0) — CALL [EAX+0x170] = TView vtable slot 0x5c (declared TView.h:130, body 0x48abe0). This is what attaches the factory-built screen tree under the TIncludeView packet, which BuildTurnEventFactoryPacket (TIncludeView.cpp:34, 0x48cf10) has already attached under mainView via mainView->AttachChildControl(this, 0). Without it the built tree is orphaned — it never joins g_pDisplayMgr->activeDialog's child list, so CMcWindow::OnPaint's recursion never reaches it and NOTHING a factory builds can ever render. This is the root cause of the still-blank frame that survived the window-factory merges.

2. if (pAnchorPoint[0] || pAnchorPoint[1]) { point = {result->field24 + anchor[0], result->field28 + anchor[1]}; result->CaptureLayoutF0(point, 0); } — CALL [EDX+0xf0] = slot 0x3c (TView.h:90). Anchor-offset reposition of the built tree.

Note the factory call itself IS faithful: original pushes literal 0 as first arg (PUSH 0x0 at 0x491cd8), so factory(0, nEventCode) is correct — only the post-loop tail is missing. InvokeDialogFactoryFromPacket (0x491d80, 85 bytes) was re-verified and matches our port (registry vtable+0x30 call, then result slots 0xd8/0xe0) — no change needed there.

Follow-up in the same change: retire the two TODO(shortcut) divergences in BuildStartupIntroBackground (src/game/turn_event_dialog_factory.cpp:81-120): (a) panel arg hardcoded 0 for InitializeUiResourceEntryFrameAndParent — real pattern reads the build-stack tail (g_UiWidgetBuildStack006a13e0 last node) as parent panel, decoded in RegisterUiResourceEntry / BuildTurnEventDialogResources_2508 (heuristics note 33); (b) the force PropagateUiResourceContextRecursive(mainNativeWindow) hack at the factory tail — original passes 0 (verified in BuildTurnOrderNavigationWindow); with the packet attach fixed, nativeWindow50 propagates through the real mechanism.

Acceptance: 0x491cc0 port matches the listing (attach + anchor tail present); both TODO(shortcut) divergences removed; just compare 0x491cc0 improves; title tree hangs off activeDialog->packet->tree (verifiable in a debugger or by the screen actually painting once the crash issue is fixed).
notes: Re-verified 2026-07-05 after merging origin/main (106 commits) + local session work: the described defect (dropped AttachChildControl call + anchor reposition) is FIXED in the current tree — src/game/TTurnEventDialogFactoryRegistry.cpp:RunRegisteredDialogFactoriesByEventCode now calls result->AttachChildControl(pEventPacket ? pEventPacket : ..., 0)-equivalent and the anchor CaptureLayoutF0 tail, matching the listing. just compare 0x491cc0 now shows 92.59% (up from a stub-level score), and the only remaining diff is a pure register-allocation/instruction-order difference (mov edx,[eax];mov eax,[edi+0x24];add edx,eax vs the reordered mov esi,[eax];mov edx,[edi+0x24];add edx,esi) — semantically identical, no logic gap. The two TODO(shortcut) sub-items in BuildStartupIntroBackground also look at least partly resolved (parent already reads g_UiWidgetBuildStack006a13e0's tail; PropagateUiResourceContextRecursive already passes 0, not a forced window). NOT independently verified: the runtime debugger/screenshot check that the title tree actually paints via activeDialog->packet->tree. Strong candidate to close once that smoke-test is done.

title: Diagnose+fix the null-function-pointer crash in the first DispatchTurnEventSlot4C dispatch
description:
Live evidence (2026-07-03, winedbg on current main build): breakpoint at recomp TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C (src/game/TViewMgr.cpp:807) hits during startup; after detaching, the process raises 'Unhandled page fault on read access to 00000000 at address 00000000' — EIP=0, i.e. a CALL through a null function pointer or a virtual call through a zeroed vptr/slot. The process stays alive (blank frame) because something swallows the fault. A breakpoint at TWindow::DispatchSlot9CToLinkedChildren (TWindow.cpp:235) was NOT hit before the crash, and no CMcWindow native window is ever created (watched X11 tree 20s) — so the crash happens between dispatch entry and mainView realization, killing the whole UI bring-up.

IMPORTANT winedbg pitfall (documented in memory turn-event-dispatch-code-mega-map): named params printed at function entry are unreliable — the bp showed eventCode=3 but raw stack reads in past sessions showed the first dispatch is actually eventCode=0 (from the DispatchUiSlot4C inline helper in TSimMgr_AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine.cpp). Verify with print *(short*)($esp+4).

Static suspects along the eventCode==0 path (TViewMgr.cpp:855-872): (a) raw write to g_pGlobalUiRootController+0x4c — null global would fault at the write EIP, not 0, so unlikely; (b) mainView->CallVoidSlotA0() — virtual slot 0x28 on the TGameWindow activeDialog; (c) CWMgrIterator walk over g_LiveViewRegistry calling window->OrphanCallChain_C2_I10_0048e120(); (d) g_pSfxPlaybackSystem->PlaySoundEffect in the sound-cue block (only when mode is 0x67-0x6a). If the first dispatch is instead 0x11f8, suspects extend to the cross-code path: g_pUiViewManager->NoOpRuntimeUiCallback_005df780, ResolveControlByTag, TIncludeView packet build, g_pDisplayMgr->LoadMainViewClipSnapshotIntoQuickDrawState, UiRuntimeSlot110 (empty body, see imperialism-decomp-key). A vtable slot that is a pure ghidra-autogen stub declared but never linked would be nonnull, so prefer the zeroed-vptr theory: an object created by an autogen stub returning malloc'd/zeroed memory instead of a real ctor.

Debug recipe: kill+settle, then DEBUG_TIMEOUT=90s WINEDEBUG=-all DEBUG_SCRIPT=$'break TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C\ncont\n<step/finish/raw-stack-reads>\nquit\n' just debug-timeout. Do NOT chain pkill+launch in one command (silently races). Winedbg breakpoints freeze the message pump — use stepping, not free-running, once inside.

Acceptance: the null call is identified and fixed with real modeled code (no stub rollback — gate-chasing guardrail applies); startup proceeds past the first dispatch without faulting; TWindow::DispatchSlot9CToLinkedChildren is reached (breakpoint hits) and a CMcWindow is constructed.

title: Bring-up roadmap: render title screen, reach main menu, enter the map
description:
Umbrella for the runnable-game bring-up path, researched 2026-07-03 (full session evidence in child issues). Current live state: recomp builds and runs stable under Wine, CMainFrame opens maximized (2560x1440) but stays 100% blank; NO CMcWindow native child window is ever created (verified by watching the X11 tree for 20s post-launch); the process page-faults calling address 0 (call through a null function pointer) shortly after the FIRST TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C dispatch fires (verified via winedbg breakpoint; the fault is currently swallowed into a hung-but-alive process).

The verified working init chain (all real code, no action needed): ImperialismApp::InitInstance -> TAmbitApplication init (src/game/TAmbitApplication.cpp:100-160) creates TSimMgr (g_pLocalizationTable), TAssetMgr (g_pUiViewManager), turn-event dialog factory registry, TViewMgr (g_pUiRuntimeContext), TDisplayMgr (g_pDisplayMgr) -> TDisplayMgr::InitializeTurnOrderNavigationDialogByViewportSize (0x4fe840, ported) resolves activeDialog = dialog factory result for event 0x7d1/0x7d2 (BuildTurnOrderNavigationWindow -> bare TGameWindow, ported) -> TMacViewMgr (g_pStrategicMapViewSystem, InitializeStrategicMapViewSystem ported) -> THelpMgr, TMultiplayerMgr. WM_COMMAND 100 -> TSimMgr::AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine (0x57da70) case 1 dispatches event 0x11f8 (title screen, factory case ported) via g_pUiRuntimeContext->DispatchTurnEventSlot4C (0x5d69e0 region, ported).

Paint architecture (solved, see memory paint-trigger-cmcwindow-onpaint): TView content paints ONLY via CMcWindow::OnPaint (0x4938c0, 100%) -> owner TWindow PaintVisibleChildrenIntersectingClipRect slot 0x43 recursion. CMcWindow is created lazily by TWindow::DispatchSlot9CToLinkedChildren (TWindow.cpp:235, ported) the first time DispatchTurnEventSlot4C runs its cross-code path on mainView (=g_pDisplayMgr->activeDialog). CIncludeView never paints TView content.

Phases: (1) fix the null-call crash in the first dispatch; (2) fix the factory-tree attach gap so built screens join the paintable tree; (3) verify title art renders in the main frame; (4) intro->menu advance chain (movie completion -> post 0x5dc); (5) port the 0x5dc menu screen factory case; (6) menu interactivity (mouse capture + command routing); (7) new-game path to the strategic map (0x7d8 family). Children track each phase with addresses and evidence.

title: Port the diplomacy turn-event call tree (prereqs for the 11.5KB state machine)
description: Parent for the delegable prerequisite groups below. TMultiplayerMgr::ProcessDiplomacyTurnStateEventStateMachine 0x545940 (bd 1uj.52) calls 44 currently-stubbed functions; its full unowned transitive closure is 147 functions / 43.6KB (measured via BFS through call targets, ILT-resolved). title: Raise TSimMgr::AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine 0x57da70 from 9.9% (core game loop)
description: The core game-loop state machine — TSimMgr::AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine 0x57da70, 4,787 bytes — is ported but scores only 9.9%, the largest low-scoring real method in the repo (it already has its own TU: TSimMgr_AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine.cpp). A 10% score on a ported state machine usually means the switch dispatch shape or the surrounding EH/loop structure is wrong, not the leaf calls. Diagnose with just compare 0x57da70 asm diff: check switch jump-table vs if-chain codegen, state-field typing, and whether callee methods it invokes are real virtuals vs casts. This function gates startup-loop map/turn-node advancement (1uj.31) and the turn-event pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Score substantially raised (or the structural blocker documented with asm-diff evidence); no architectural regressions; build/gates/stats pass.
notes:
Progress 2026-07-02: raised score 9.9%/10.11% -> 10.47%; more importantly fixed
real structural bugs (not just score-chasing):

1. Function-scope CString hoisting (heuristics.md #33): original constructs a
   CString unconditionally right after the prologue (0x57da8e), not inside case
   2's loop where the port had it. That local's non-trivial dtor is what forces
   MSVC to emit ONE shared epilogue that every case's `break` jumps to, instead
   of duplicating pop/ret at every exit. Moving the local to function scope
   shrank the recomp/original byte-size gap from +62 bytes to +1 byte
   (1277->1116 vs original's 1215) before any other fix landed.

2. Case 3 had three free-function stubs standing in for real __thiscall TSimMgr
   methods reached through ILT thunks (heuristics.md #34):

not fix it. Recorded here so a future session can pick one up as its own decomp-loop pass:

- **`SelectBestMapActionContextForNationDiplomacyMask`** (0x560e70, 197 bytes) — `__thiscall`

is probably reusable elsewhere), (2) the `IsZoneMaskOrArrayEntryPresentForKey`/

# TGreatPower blockers

Living register for `TGreatPower::vftable` (orig `0x00653938`, 184 slots) recovery.
Scores and commands go in commit messages; structural blockers and decisions live here.

## Baseline (2026-06-16, refreshed after `2366322`)

| Check | Result |

| `just vtable TGreatPower` | **100% match** (deep-slot alignment complete, including `vtable+0xfc` and `vtable+0x2ac`) |
| Orig vtable | `0x00653938`, slots `0x00`–`0xb7` (184); `0xb3`–`0xb7` NULL |
| Recomp vtable | `0x00468648` |
| Architecture | `TGreatPower : public TObject` |

### Canary `just compare` scores

| `0x4d89d0` | `GetTGreatPowerClassNamePointer` / slot 0 | 50% |

| `0x4da500` | `SerializeNationOrderStateToArchive` | 95% |

### Prefix/lifecycle summary

`TGreatPower` now uses the expected inherited prefix:
- `vtable+0x00`: `GetRuntimeClass` (`0x4d89d0`)
- `vtable+0x04`: scalar deleting dtor (`0x4d8c20`, `// SYNTHETIC`)
- `vtable+0x08..0x10`: inherited `Serialize`/`AssertValid`/`Dump`
- `vtable+0x14..0x1c`: `WriteTo`/`ReadFrom`/`Free`

---

## Blocker register

| ID | Blocker | Status | Unblocks |
|----|---------|--------|----------|
| B1 | **Deep-table drift** beyond lifecycle prefix (`vtable+0x68+` and selected auto overrides) | resolved on base | Full 100% `TGreatPower` vtable alignment |
| B2 | **`TGREATPOWER_VTABLE_SLOT` macro** emitted competing empty bodies | resolved | macro deleted; slots promoted to named virtuals |
| B3 | **NULL orig tail slots** (`0xb3`–`0xb7`): C++ virtuals inflate recomp vtable | resolved on base | TAutoGreatPower owns tail via `EscalateNeedSlot2C8`/`CallSlotB3` |
| B4 | **Layout tail `0x964+`** — `missionQueue`/`mapNodeStateFlags` on base, alloc derived `0xb64` | open | `just stackcmp 0x4d89f0` shows ctor epilogue structural mismatch; `offsetof` probes pass, `ASSERT_SIZE(0x964)` deferred |

| B9 | **Declaration-order drift** — some virtuals (e.g. `AssignNeedSlotFromSourceSlot19C`) sit mid-table but map to high indices (`0x19c`); comment labels ≠ slot indices | resolved on base | Full 100% match after stub sweep |

## Decisions (do not regress)

1. **Keep `public TObject` on `TGreatPower`** — this is now the settled architecture.
2. **Slot 0** — `GetRuntimeClass()` virtual owns `0x4d89d0`; remove duplicate cdecl helper.

design:
# Handoff: porting TMission's children

**Status as of commit `fea362b`** ("Model TMission as a real 39-slot polymorphic
base"). The base `TMission` class now exists as a real polymorphic C++ class. Your job
is to port its subclasses on top of it. Read this whole doc first, plus memory
`tmission-vtable-layout-ground-truth.md` (the authoritative layout/ownership record).

## What is already done (the base)

- `include/game/TMission.h` — `class TMission : public TObject` (so `CObject <- TObject
  <- TMission`). `// VTABLE: IMPERIALISM 0x0065a4e8`, size `0x14`.
  - Fields: `nationId04` (short @0x04), `pathMarker06` (short @0x06), `state08` (byte
    @0x08), `value0c` (int @0x0c), `flag10` (byte @0x10), `marker11` (byte @0x11).
  - 39 virtuals declared in **exact** vtable slot order, slots `0x00-0x26`. Slot
    addresses are in the trailing comment on each line.
  - Slots `0x27-0x2f` are **NULL** in the base table (abstract region). **Not
    declared** on TMission — C++ pure virtuals would emit `_purecall`, not NULL. Derived
    classes append their own virtuals starting at slot `0x27` (see below).
  - `TMissionNodeCallback` (unrelated small interface) also lives in this header — leave
    it.
- `src/game/TMission.cpp` — real ctor `0x535020`, dtor `0x535080`, SYNTHETIC scalar
  deleting dtor `0x535050`, `GetRuntimeClass` `0x534fb0`, and all 37 own-slot bodies.
  - The 16 trivial slot stubs were **relocated out of `noop_slots.cpp`** into real
    methods here. Do not re-add them to noop_slots.
  - `CreateByKindAndNodeContext` (factory `0x5350d0`) still **forwards to the thunk** —
    leave it until the concrete ctors use real inheritance (then do plan step 4).
- `src/game/global_data_tables.cpp` — `PTR_s_TMission_00697848` (RTTI descriptor) and
  `g_MissionDefaultScore_0065a468` (float 0.0, the slot 0x68-0x7C constant).

## The hierarchy to build (single inheritance, MSVC)

```
CObject <- TObject <- TMission        (done)
  TNavyMission   : TMission           vtable 0x65a818, 54 slots, alloc 0x3c
    TControlSeaZoneMission            alloc 0x3c
    TEscortMission                    alloc 0x3c
    TBlockadePortMission              alloc 0x40 (+0x3c extra ptr)
    TBeachheadMission                 alloc 0x40 (navy-shaped child of invade)
    TScatteredShipsMission            unnamed vtable @0x65a5a8
  TArmyMission   : TMission           vtable 0x65ad38, alloc 0x20 list @+0x18
    TAttackProvinceMission            alloc 0x34 (+0x30/+0x32 shorts)
    TDefendProvinceMission            vtable 0x65a680
    TInvadeMission                    alloc 0x38 (+0x34 beachhead ptr)
```

Inheritance is confirmed structurally (vtable prefix-sharing + ctor sequencing), NOT by
name. Re-verify each edge before adding it (Hard Rule 12): the derived ctor calls
`ConstructTMission`/the parent ctor then installs its own vtable, and the derived vtable
shares the base slot skeleton with selective overrides.

### Layout gotcha: paired vtables

Each mission class has TWO adjacent vtables in `.rdata`: a 12-slot
`g_vtblMissionOrderPrioritizer<X>` companion (a **separate** helper class — do NOT fold
it into the mission vtable) immediately before the main `g_vtbl<X>`. Full address map is
in the memory note.

## Recommended order (per plan)

1. **`TNavyMission : TMission`** and **`TArmyMission : TMission`** first — they explain
   most offsets. Model each as a real class; ctor calls the base ctor; declare the
   appended virtuals (slots `0x27+`) in exact order. Get vtable + ctor/dtor +
   scalar-deleting dtor pairing.
   - Note: the current `include/game/TNavyMission.h` / `src/game/TNavyMission.cpp` is a
     *standalone* class holding only two static scoring helpers
     (`ComputeOrderDistributionSimilarityScore*`). Fold those into the real
     `TNavyMission : TMission` (keep the addresses/markers).
2. The simplest concrete ctors (`TControlSeaZoneMission`, `TEscortMission`,
   `TAttackProvinceMission`, `TInvadeMission`, `TBeachheadMission`) — ctors first to
   establish sizes/vtables/fields.
3. Then `CreateByKindAndNodeContext` real switch (factory `0x5350d0`; the autogen body
   is in `src/ghidra_autogen/global_part011.cpp` ~line 11260, cases by mission kind).
4. Then serializers (`SerializeTArmyMission`/`DeserializeTArmyMission`,
   `SerializeTNavyMissionCommon`/`DeserializeTNavyMissionCommon`), then scoring.

## Workflow (per class)

`just ghidra-vtable-dump`, then resolve slot bodies with the thunk-resolver pattern used
in commit fea362b (see below). Map every slot to its body address + name, declare
virtuals in order, port bodies. Then:
`just sync-ownership` → `just regen-stubs` → `just build` → `just detect` →
`just compare 0xADDR` → `just gates` + `just format <files>`. Commit on `main`.

Thunk→body resolver (read-only), run with `.env` loaded:
```
just ghidra-vtable-dump <Class> 0x<vtable> > /tmp/vt.csv   # then JMP-follow entry_addr
```
(The inline resolver script used for the base is reproducible from
`tools/ghidra/create_vtable_body_functions.py`'s `resolve()`; load `.env` so
`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` is set, and run with `PYTHONPATH=.`.)

## KNOWN OPEN ISSUE — the base vtable reports 0.00%

The recomp `TMission::vftable` is structurally **correct** (right functions, right order;
verified in the compare diff), and **37/39 slot bodies match 100% individually**. But
`just compare 0x0065a4e8` reports the vftable as 0.00% similar.

Diagnosis so far:
- The diff shows every orig slot as a thunk (`0x40xxxx`, the ILT jmp table) with
  "no recomp", and every recomp slot as a body — i.e. reccmp is not aligning the two
  lists at all (full `-`/`+`, no LCS match).
- This is **not** simply "orig uses thunks": TControl's orig vtable also uses `0x40xxxx`
  thunks and matches 100%, so reccmp *can* resolve vtable thunks.
- Recomp side shows 3 genuinely-unpaired slots: `0x01` scalar-deleting dtor ("no orig" —
  SYNTHETIC not pairing), `0x02` Seritalize (recomp inherits `CObject::Serialize`
  `0x412bd0` but orig wants `TEventHandler::Serialize` `0x485e90` — a COMDAT-folded
  shared body), and `0x08`/`0x09` generic forwarders (`0x4798d0` TZone / `0x415ce0`
  TEventHandler) that did **not** linker-fold (got own recomp addresses, "no orig").

Hypotheses to chase (not yet resolved — user deferred it):
1. The all-`-`/all-`+` total misalignment smells like reccmp matching by raw pointer and
   not thunk-resolving the orig side *for the % computation* in this particular case —
   possibly tied to the "ILT thunk retirement / reccmp fork branch awaiting push" note
   in memory. Compare against a known-good vtable's internals to see whether its recomp
   slots are thunks vs bodies.

Partial trace 2026-07-02 (part 4, IAT resolved, still not committed -- no code
changes, research only): resolved the two IAT calls in
CreateFontFromPresetAndAttachRegionHandle 0x494130 via Ghidra's external-symbol
table: dword ptr [0x6ab12c] = KERNEL32.dll!lstrcpynA, dword ptr [0x6aad7c] =
GDI32.dll!CreateFontIndirectA. Confirms it's a real CFont factory: new CFont(),
populate a LOGFONT-shaped stack buffer, lstrcpynA a face-name string into it,
CreateFontIndirectA(&logfont) -> HFONT, then CALL 0x613a4c on the CFont (ecx=
CFont*) to attach the handle (likely CFont::Attach or CFont::CreateFontIndirect
wrapping the two steps -- not confirmed which).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT for whoever picks this up: the ESP+0x10 stack region is used
BOTH as an apparent lookup table (populated with sequential values 1..8 at
[esp+0x14..0x30], then indexed via `MOV EBP,[ESP+EAX*4+0x10]` using
styleDescriptor->field4 as the index) AND handed directly to CreateFontIndirectA
as the LOGFONT* pointer (`LEA EDX,[ESP+0x10]; PUSH EDX` before the
CreateFontIndirectA call). This means the "lookup table" values are actually
pre-populated LOGFONT field defaults (lfWidth=1, lfEscapement=2, ... or similar
-- the field mapping is NOT yet verified against the real LOGFONTA layout) that
get selectively overwritten later based on styleDescriptor->field0 (clamped to
0-4, likely a font-family index used for a face-name lookup at
g_something[esi*4+0x695108]) and field4 (the size hint from
BuildUiTextStyleDescriptor's arg2). Do NOT assume a naive sequential mapping
without carefully cross-checking every write against the real LOGFONTA struct
offsets (lfHeight@0,lfWidth@4,lfEscapement@8,lfOrientation@c,lfWeight@10,
lfItalic@14,lfUnderline@15,lfStrikeOut@16,lfCharSet@17,lfOutPrecision@18,
lfClipPrecision@19,lfQuality@1a,lfPitchAndFamily@1b,lfFaceName@1c[32]) -- a
sequential 1,2,3...8 fill doesn't obviously correspond to sane LOGFONT defaults,
so there may be an intermediate indirection I haven't traced (e.g. the table
might be UNRELATED scratch space for a DIFFERENT purpose that happens to share
the stack slot with the zeroed LOGFONT region due to compiler stack reuse across
non-overlapping lifetimes -- very plausible given SUB ESP,0x64 reserves 100
bytes, more than one LOGFONT needs).

Given the precision required to get font construction semantically right (a
wrong LOGFONT field mapping is a silent bug, not a crash), did not attempt a
port this session -- recommend the next session start fresh with
`just ghidra-listing 0x494130` and step through byte-by-byte with the LOGFONTA
field table open side by side, ideally verifying against Mac CodeWarrior
oracle evidence if a comparable Mac font-creation function exists.

title: Audit E: turn-event-code coverage matrix — the screen-by-screen completion map
description:
Every game screen is addressed by a turn-event code (0x11f8 title, 0x5dc menu, 0x7d1/0x7d2 root window, 0x7d8-0x7de map/industry family, 0x23f7-0x2508 dialogs, ...). Nobody currently knows the full code inventory or which codes are end-to-end functional. Build the matrix once, mechanically, and keep it regenerable.

Enumerate codes from four sources: (1) the ported DispatchTurnEventSlot4C switch arms (src/game/TViewMgr.cpp:807-1013 — parse source or just read the listing at the original); (2) the HandleTurnStateExitAndPostFollowupEventCode jump table (0x5db6fc targets / 0x5db710 index bytes, 0x18 cases — each posts a code); (3) each of the 17 registered factories' range-check/jump-table headers (e.g. 0x459548 inside 0x4538a0; note Ghidra mis-bounds several of these — use just ghidra-raw-disasm across gaps, and repair bounds per 1uj.51.1/1uj.29); (4) constant-scan of DispatchTurnEventSlot4C/PostTurnEventCodeMessage2420 callsites for immediate code operands (the global-xref-oracle constant-mining pattern in tools/reccmp/global_xref_oracle.py is the template).

Per code, emit columns: sender(s) (which state-machine case / exit-table case / command handler posts it), owning factory + per-case handler address + port status, TViewMgr per-code hook (the TViewMgr.cpp:942-1010 switch: UiRuntimeSlotXX name + empty/ported status, cross-ref Audit B), teardown hook (the curCode switch at TViewMgr.cpp:833-853), and screen identity where known (bitmap ids via docs/reference/bitmap-ids.md, class names). This matrix is the top-level progress instrument for the whole bring-up epic: 1uj.57's phases each 'light up' rows, and the remaining dark rows ARE the remaining UI work, quantified. It also de-risks porting order decisions (e.g. it will show which codes the 0x5db620 exit table can actually reach from the states a fresh boot traverses, so nobody ports an unreachable screen first).

title: Audit D: data-section function-pointer scan — registered callbacks and dispatch tables with zero code xrefs
description:
Functions referenced only from DATA never show up in call-graph reasoning: FUN_00484230 (the movie-done hook that advances intro->menu, found in 1uj.57.4 research) has ZERO code xrefs — it is registered as a raw pointer at runtime and reached via a message/callback dispatch. There is an unknown population of these across the UI system (timer procs, window-proc hooks, MCI/mmio callbacks, sort comparators, factory tables).

Scan (extend tools/ghidra/, or a new dump_data_funcptrs.py): iterate initialized data blocks (.data/.rdata), read every aligned dword (per-byte getByte or Java-side scan — NOT bulk jpype getBytes, known silent-zero bug), keep values that are entry points of defined functions (or ILT thunks -> resolve to targets). Classify each hit by container: (1) inside a known VTABLE range (drop — Audit A territory); (2) inside an AFX_MSGMAP entry (drop — Audit C); (3) inside a CRuntimeClass (pfnCreateObject — drop, rtti-oracle covers); (4) everything else = callback/table candidate. For each candidate: dump the surrounding data region shape (array of pointers? struct with the pointer at fixed offset?), the target's ownership/score/size, and the data address's own xrefs (who reads the table = the dispatcher).

Also the runtime-registration variant that a data scan cannot see: functions whose ADDRESS is taken in CODE (PUSH imm32 / MOV reg,imm32 where imm is a function entry) but that have no CALL xrefs — Ghidra models these as from-references; query them (xrefs_to already surfaces the distinction — filter reference type != CALL). This is how FUN_00484230's registration site will be found (search code for 0x00484230 as immediate).

Deliverable: ranked list (UI-relevant first: target in the 0x41xxxx-0x5exxxx game range, unported, original size > 32B) of callback registrations with their dispatcher context, folded into the ui-gap-report output. Known validation case: must find FUN_00484230 and its registration site; should also rediscover kStartupFactories (the 17-entry factory table) as a positive control.

Acceptance: tool committed; validation cases found; UI-relevant unported callbacks triaged into port issues.

title: Audit C: MFC message-map enumeration — port status of every WM_/custom-message handler
description:
The UI runs on MFC message maps as much as on vtables, and message-map handlers are invisible to vtable audits. Custom messages already known load-bearing: 0x2420 (turn-event post — handler unlocated, needed by 1uj.57.4), 0x4ef (packet context propagation, handler 0x482c1c on CIncludeView), 0x468 (CMcWindow show/hide state), 0x36a (deferred CMcWindow handler), plus standard WM_PAINT/WM_LBUTTON*/WM_CHAR etc.

Enumeration recipe (new committed tool tools/ghidra/dump_message_maps.py + just target): for each of the 471 CRuntimeClass descriptors (rtti-oracle), the owning class's GetMessageMap override is a trivial getter ('MOV EAX, imm32; RET') — read the imm to get the AFX_MSGMAP {pBaseMap, pEntries}; walk pEntries as 24-byte AFX_MSGMAP_ENTRY records (nMessage,nCode,nID,nLastID,nSig,pfn) to the zero sentinel. Alternative/cross-check: scan .rdata directly for entry-shaped records (the 0x4ef hunt found CIncludeView's map at 0x6481e8 this way, with the owning CRuntimeClass exactly 0x18 bytes earlier — see memory turn-event-dispatch-code-mega-map 2026-07-01-E). PITFALL: do NOT use bulk jpype Memory.getBytes (silently returns zeros); use Java-side Memory.findBytes or per-byte getByte — documented in tools/ghidra/raw_disasm.py.

Known-good validation targets: CMcWindow map @ 0x64b5e8 (14 entries @ 0x64b5f0, WM_PAINT->OnPaint 0x4938c0), CIncludeView map @ 0x6481e8 (14 entries, includes 0x4ef->0x482c1c, and NO WM_PAINT — the audit must reproduce both facts).

title: Upstream reccmp fix: exclude .claude/worktrees/ from source dir walk
description:
Port a local session patch to the real fork repo (https://github.com/agluszak/reccmp.git)
so it survives `uv sync` instead of being silently lost.

Symptom: while a Claude Code agent runs in an isolated git worktree under
.claude/worktrees/<id>/ (a full checkout of this repo, containing its own
copy of every source file with the same // FUNCTION:/// VTABLE:/// GLOBAL:
markers), any reccmp tool that scans "all source" (decomplint, compare,
vtable, stats, gates) sees every marker address TWICE -- once in the real
tree, once in the worktree copy -- and its duplicate-address dedup logic
kicks in, dropping annotations and/or producing wildly wrong aggregate
results (observed: hundreds of spurious "Dropped duplicate address... VTABLE
annotation" errors, and a `just vtable` run reporting 309/397 "not matching"
when the real number was 0).

Root cause: reccmp/dir.py::walk_source_dir() uses a raw os.walk() with no
exclusion logic at all -- no .gitignore awareness, no worktree awareness.

Local patch applied this session (in .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/
reccmp/dir.py, NOT persisted -- lost on next `uv sync`/reinstall):

    def walk_source_dir(source: Path, *, recursive: bool = True) -> Iterator[Path]:
        """Returns any C/C++ source code files found in the given directory tree."""

        # Python 3.12 introduced Path.walk(). We use os.walk() instead for broader compatibility.
        for subdir, dirnames, files in os.walk(source.absolute()):
            # skip nested git worktrees (e.g. .claude/worktrees/<id>/), which
            # otherwise contain duplicate copies of every source file and register
            # every marker address twice, corrupting the duplicate-address dedup
            # logic in compare/ingest.py.
            dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if os.path.join(subdir, d).find("/worktrees/") == -1]
            for file in files:
                path = Path(os.path.join(subdir, file))
                if is_file_c_like(path):
                    yield path

            if not recursive:
                break

Verified working: `just gates` went from EXIT 1 (contaminated) to EXIT 0
clean with a live worktree agent still running throughout; `just stats`
subsequently reported "dropped duplicate addresses: 0" for the first time
all session.

Consider a more general fix than the literal "/worktrees/" substring match --
e.g. respecting .gitignore, or using `git ls-files` instead of os.walk()
entirely when running inside a git repo (would also naturally exclude
build-*/ output dirs, vendor/ caches, etc. without needing to enumerate every
exclusion pattern by name).

title: Recover the true TToolBarCluster map-interaction subclass (this+0x94..0xbc field owner)
description:
SetMapInteractionMode (0x596cb0), RefreshMapOrderEntryPanel (0x597810), SetActiveMapOrderEntry (0x597950), and their whole caller cluster (TryHandleMapContextAction 0x55a020, TrySelectNextValidMapOrderEntry 0x5998a0, CycleMapInteractionSelectionAfterHandledClick 0x597a80, SelectNextValidMapOrderEntryFromCursor 0x599770, ResetMapInteractionToCivilianMode 0x5999f0, OpenMapEntryOrderDialog 0x597f80, GetActiveMapOrderEntry 0x5979f0, RunNavyPrimaryOrderCreationDialogAndApplyResults 0x598e10) are currently attributed to TToolBarCluster in config/symbols.csv, but that attribution is measurably wrong: TToolBarCluster's real object size is verified as exactly 0x88 bytes (TToolBarCluster::CreateObject @ 0x584d80 pushes 0x88 to its allocator call; RTTI oracle agrees; no class derives from TToolBarCluster in config/rtti_class_oracle.csv). The disassembly of this cluster reads/writes this+0x94 (byte flag), this+0x96 (short 'interaction mode', same convention as TIconBar's own +0x96 field), this+0x98 (pointer), and a 3-element pointer array at this+0xb0..0xbc on the SAME receiver (confirmed via self-recursive calls between SetMapInteractionMode/RefreshMapOrderEntryPanel/SetActiveMapOrderEntry) -- all past the verified 0x88-byte footprint.

Ruled out TIconSlider (size 0xbc=188, tempting exact match for the 0xb0..0xbc bound) via its own ctor (0x5062d0): it zero-inits a single dword at +0xb0 plus two separate WORD fields at +0xb4/+0xb6, not a 3-element pointer array. TIconBar (0x9c bytes) does have a confirmed WORD setter at +0x96 (TIconBar::OrphanTiny_SetWordEcxOffset_96_005060f0) but is too small for the +0xb0..0xbc array. No RTTI-registered class satisfies both constraints (TCluster/TControl-vtable-shaped so it can share the +0x94 ResolveControlByTag dispatch slot, AND >= 0xc0 bytes).

Most likely explanation: a further-derived, RTTI-invisible subclass of TToolBarCluster (never registered via DECLARE_DYNCREATE/IMPLEMENT_DYNCREATE, so absent from config/rtti_class_oracle.csv), hand-instantiated directly rather than through the DYNCREATE factory. Needs a dedicated class-recovery pass (see class-recovery skill): find the real constructor (writes vtable + inits this+0x94..0xbc), confirm its size, and re-home these methods there before porting their bodies.

Currently unblocked/parked in TWorldView.cpp via a scoped TMapOrderToolbarPendingState typed-view struct (Hard Rule 8's 'typed view struct' option) instead of claiming these offsets as TToolBarCluster members -- see bd 1uj.50 notes for the CreateObject regression evidence that forced this.

title: Repo-wide glob scanners pick up .claude/worktrees/ contents (breaks concurrent worktree-isolated agents)
description:
Discovered 2026-07-02 while running `just compare 0x4e1f40` with two other
agents concurrently working in `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` subdirectories
(spawned via the Agent tool's isolation: "worktree" option, which places
worktrees inside the main repo tree at .claude/worktrees/<id>).

Symptom: `just compare` (and presumably `just gates`, `just stats`, any tool
that scans for markers/symbols across the whole repo) emitted a wall of
"Dropped duplicate address 0x... on VTABLE annotation in file:
.claude/worktrees/agent-.../include/game/*.h" errors and produced a bloated
(4.3MB) diff output, because the same VTABLE/FUNCTION-marked header exists
both in the main tree and in each agent's worktree checkout.

Root cause: repo-wide scanner tools use raw filesystem globs (e.g.
tools/workflow/prune_ilt_thunks.py's collect_claimed_addresses does
`glob.glob(str(repo_root / pattern), recursive=True)` over `src/**/*.cpp`
and `include/**/*.h`) rather than a git-aware file listing (`git ls-files`),
so they don't know to exclude .claude/worktrees/ (which is presumably
gitignored, since it's runtime state, but glob.glob doesn't consult
.gitignore).

This doesn't just affect prune_ilt_thunks.py -- likely affects every
tools/workflow/*.py and tools/ghidra/*.py script using the same
glob.glob(repo_root / "src/**/*.cpp") pattern (marker collection for
antipattern-gate, marker-gate, symbols integrity check, vtable-gate,
reccmp's own marker scan for // GLOBAL:/// FUNCTION:/// VTABLE: comments,
etc.) -- anywhere that scans "all manual source" by filesystem glob rather
than `git ls-files` or an explicit exclude for .claude/worktrees.

Impact: any session running gates/compare/stats while a worktree-isolated
subagent is active gets spurious duplicate-marker errors, and worse,
"dropping" one of the duplicates could silently pick the WRONG one (the
in-progress worktree copy instead of the committed main-tree copy, or
vice versa), corrupting results without obvious signal beyond the noisy
warnings.

Fix: audit tools/workflow/*.py and tools/ghidra/*.py for raw glob.glob()
repo-wide scans and either (a) switch to `git ls-files` filtering to
tracked files only, or (b) add an explicit exclude for paths containing
'.claude/worktrees/' (or more generally, anything under .claude/ or listed
in .gitignore). Prefer (a) if these tools don't need to see uncommitted
changes in the main tree either way; (b) if they do.

Not blocking any specific decomp task -- filed as infra debt discovered
opportunistically. Only matters when running gates/compare/stats
concurrently with worktree-isolated agents (the Agent tool's
isolation: "worktree" option, or manual `just`-adjacent worktree use).
notes:
Repo-tool audit (2026-07-02): audited every glob.glob()/rglob() scanner in tools/workflow/*.py and tools/ghidra/*.py. Finding: they ALL scan BOUNDED roots (src/**, include/**, src/game/**, or a passed-in source_dir like src/game) — none scans from repo_root with a fully-recursive descent, so none can actually reach .claude/worktrees/<id>/ (which lives under .claude/, not under src/ or include/). prune_ilt_thunks.py's glob.glob(repo_root/'src/**/*.cpp') is anchored at src/ and is likewise safe. So the repo-side tools were NOT the vector; the only real vector is reccmp's own walk_source_dir (bd 7hi, upstream).

Defensive hardening applied anyway (commit pending) so a future mis-rooted scan (root='.'/repo_root) stays correct: added is_excluded_scan_path() to tools/common/file_scan.py (excludes any path with a .claude component) and wired it into iter_files() plus the two gate scanners that roll their own rglob (check_construction_antipatterns.collect_files, check_no_raw_vtable_calls.collect_files). 59 tooling tests + antipattern-gate + vtable-gate all still exit 0.

Keeping idi OPEN per its own guidance: the actionable real fix is 7hi (reccmp dir.py, upstream fork push). Close idi once 7hi lands upstream and the dep is bumped.

title: Eliminate 20 oversized recomp vtables (over-hoisted virtuals)
description: just vtable reports 'Recomp vtable is larger than orig vtable' for 20 classes even though slot content is 100%: TWindow, TFloatWindow, TMinor, TRearFloatWindow, TDlgWindow, TMacViewMgr, TMapMgr, TMapMaker, TScatteredShipsMission, TControlSeaZoneMission, TEscortMission, TBeachheadMission, TBlockadePortMission, TRemoteMinor, TZoneSecondaryNeighborStretch, TOcean, TPlacard, TNumberedArrowButton, TCivUnit, TViewMgr. An oversized recomp vtable means the source class declares virtuals the original class does not have — usually a virtual over-hoisted into a base that only some siblings own (see the minister-vtable-family lesson), or an override declared on the wrong level of the hierarchy. Audit each class: dump the orig vtable extent, find which trailing/extra slots the recomp adds, and move those virtuals down to the classes that actually own them. Watch the TGreatPower TU codegen fragility when touching shared headers.
acceptance_criteria: just vtable emits no oversized-vtable warnings, or each remaining one is documented with the concrete blocker; vtables stay 100%; stats show no function regressions.
notes:
STATUS: 17/20 fixed, 3 documented blockers. just vtable/just gates green (100% match, all content pairs); just stats: no regressions, +1 aligned function, average similarity +0.01pp; baseline updated.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (not what the ticket description assumed): almost none of these were "virtual over-hoisted into the wrong base" bugs. The real root cause in 15/17 fixed cases was stale/junk `global` rows in config/symbols.csv (zero-consumer Ghidra auto-labels, e.g. duplicate `CMcWindow::vftable` guesses, `g_apfn*DispatchHandlers`, `g_vtblMissionOrderPrioritizer*`, a stray `TPortZone::vftable` duplicate) sitting a few bytes INSIDE a class's real (larger) vtable range. reccmp computes each vtable's "max size" as the distance to the next curated entity in its DB; an unclaimed junk row there makes reccmp think the class's vtable is much shorter than it really is, so genuinely-correct C++ (100%-matching content) gets flagged "larger than orig" even though nothing is wrong with the header. Fix = delete the junk symbols.csv row (sync-pipeline skill's documented "junk label row" pattern), not touch the class model at all.

Two classes needed real header-model fixes:
- TMapMaker: orig vtable has a literal mid-table NULL run (slots 0x22-0x28) that MSVC500 can't represent as a declared virtual (pure or not — `=0` still emits a real _purecall slot). Same pattern already documented/fixed for TZone. Fix: stop declaring virtuals past the last real slot (0x21); the two real slots after the NULL run (SetEnabled/SetState) become ordinary non-virtual methods, paired by address marker only.
- TZoneSecondaryNeighborStretch: the shared `stretch<T,Tag>` template declared both GetOrAppendUnique and Add as pure virtual, but direct memory evidence (TZoneSecondaryNeighborStretch's vtable @0x65c748 is followed 4 bytes later by TZonePrimaryNeighborStretch's vtable @0x65c74c) proves Secondary's real vtable is exactly 1 slot (GetOrAppendUnique only). Add is only ever called on the concrete type (TZone.h: primaryNeighbors.Add/secondaryNeighbors.Add), never polymorphically. Fix: demoted Add to an ordinary (non-virtual) template member in stretch.h; both Primary and Secondary now declare their own non-virtual Add.

One false-start self-corrected: initially mis-fixed TOcean by assuming its Free() wasn't real (based on the same "junk row" pattern elsewhere), but direct memory dump proved TOcean::Free IS a real override (TObject genuinely declares Free/ShallowClone/ShallowFree as its own virtuals) — the actual bug was the stray TPortZone::vftable duplicate row. Reverted the wrong header edit, fixed the real symbols.csv row instead.

FIXED (17): TWindow, TFloatWindow, TRearFloatWindow, TDlgWindow, TMinor, TRemoteMinor, TMacViewMgr, TMapMgr, TCivUnit, TMapMaker, TOcean, TScatteredShipsMission, TControlSeaZoneMission, TEscortMission, TBeachheadMission, TBlockadePortMission, TZoneSecondaryNeighborStretch.

BLOCKED — entangled with bd 1uj.54 (2): TPlacard, TNumberedArrowButton. Confirmed via reccmp's own size computation (not guesswork): TPlacard's real orig vtable boundary is only 8 slots (32 bytes) before the next class's vtable, but our header — correctly, per the shared 184-slot TControl/TAmtBar family shape — declares 116 slots; TNumberedArrowButton is 32 real slots vs 113 declared. Both sit inside the same unresolved giant TControl-family vtable block 1uj.54 is scoped to reconstruct; not a tractable few-slot fix here.

NEEDS FOLLOW-UP (1): TViewMgr — filed as bd kdm. The oversize warning WAS caused by a stale symbols.csv junk row (66f16c|g_TViewMgrTurnEventDispatchTable, zero consumers) exactly like the other 15, but deleting it exposes a real, pre-existing PAIRING gap: ~28 slots in range 0x60-0x110 currently point to placeholder stub overrides instead of the real Ghidra-identified orig functions (HandleTurnEventDialogFactorySlot70..80, InvokeStrategicMapViewMethod5C/60/68/6C/70/74, HandleTurnEvent2260_RefreshMainHudTitles, etc. — full list in bd kdm). That's a genuine porting job (~28 functions), out of scope for this vtable-size ticket, so the junk row was restored to keep just vtable/just gates green; bd kdm tracks removing it for real once those slots are ported.

Leaving this bead open (in_progress) — 3 of 20 remain, each with a concrete documented blocker per the acceptance criteria's "or each remaining one is documented with the concrete blocker" clause.

The 3 remaining are each documented with a concrete blocker per the acceptance's alternative clause: TPlacard + TNumberedArrowButton are entangled with the 184-slot TControl/TAmtBar family reconstruction (tracked in bd 1uj.54); TViewMgr's junk row hides a ~28-slot pairing gap (tracked in bd kdm). just vtable = 100% match, gates green, no stats regressions.

title: TMinor object size mismatch: ASSERT_SIZE 0x2cc vs RTTI 0x2dc
description: just class-size-check reports the only mismatch in the repo: include/game/TMinor.h asserts 0x2cc but the RTTI CRuntimeClass descriptor says m_nObjectSize=0x2dc — 0x10 bytes of fields are missing from the model. Recover the missing 0x10-byte region from ctor/dtor and member-access evidence in Ghidra, place the fields at the correct offsets (declaration order matters), and fix the ASSERT_SIZE.
acceptance_criteria: just class-size-check reports 0 mismatches; TMinor ASSERT_SIZE 0x2dc with fields evidenced from disassembly; build+gates+stats pass with no regressions.
notes:
Investigation 2026-07-02 (no fix committed yet -- documenting what's ruled out):

Confirmed via just class-size-check: TMinor is the only ASSERT_SIZE mismatch
in the repo (0x2cc vs RTTI 0x2dc, missing 0x10 bytes). TRemoteMinor (a
zero-added-fields subclass) already correctly asserts 0x2dc, corroborating
that TMinor itself must be 0x2dc -- strong second source of truth.

Ruled out:
- TMinor::TMinor() ctor (0x4e3710, real listing) only constructs 2 CString
  fields at +0x4/+0x8 and sets vtables -- doesn't touch anything near the
  tail, and doesn't even call TCountry's ctor explicitly (likely inlined).
  Reveals nothing about the missing bytes.
- TMinor::ReadFrom/WriteTo (0x4e41c0/0x4e4390) only serialize up to offset
  ~0x16a (recurringGrantByResource's region); relationGrantLinkMatrix (0x1fa)
  and everything after are NOT touched by these -- so serialization order
  doesn't reveal the tail either.
- No manual .cpp file (grep across src/game/*.cpp) does raw offset-cast
  access into TMinor/TCountry in the 0x1f0-0x2e0 range.
- Mac CodeWarrior oracle (vendor/macos_codewarrior/evidence/classes.csv) lists
  TMinor methods NOT present in our Windows model at all: AddNoticeFrom,
  AddOfferFrom, AddProvince, BecomeProtectorateOf, ChangeArmyOwnership,
  ConvertCapitolToTown, DeportCiviliansIn, GetAmtUnsold, GetStockpile,
  GetTradeOffersFor, InitializeTradeStatus, KillBoycottedForeignCompanies,
  KillEnemyCiviliansIn, LoseProvince -- these sound exactly like the kind of
  per-nation trade/notice/offer state that could occupy the missing bytes
  AND the suspiciously-large 0xd2-byte "minorTailPad1fa" blob already in the
  header (which is almost certainly NOT pure padding either -- it's 210

  evidence is name-oracle only -- checked config/symbols.csv for any

  accounted for through slot 0x34; these trade methods, if they exist on

write TCountry+0x1fa..TCountry+0x2dc (equivalently TMinor's own +0x1fa..+0x2dc

TCountry-prefix-relative). A struct-field-access-aware Ghidra script (not
available in current tooling -- xrefs_to.py only finds xrefs to a single
address, not xrefs to a class-relative field offset across many instances)
would find this fast. Absent that, would need to manually walk suspect
still-stubbed autogen functions near the 0x4d0000-0x4f0000 TMinor/TCountry
address cluster looking for offset math in the 0x1fa-0x2dc range.

title: Continue staged retail-MFC migration
description: From docs/reference/mfc-migration-plan.md. Continue staged migration from hand-rolled MFC-adjacent code to retail MSVC500 MFC 4.2 via nafxcw.lib and // LIBRARY markers. Current state: CObject/signature prep mostly done; CString reclaimed; CPtrList/CPtrArray/CObList and CArchive/CMapPtrToPtr partial; CWnd/CDC GUI surface pending and needs CWinApp/AfxWinInit scaffolding. Use real MFC APIs/classes, not modeled internals. Track reccmp delta per stage and keep each increment green.
design:
# Retail-MFC migration plan

Proven viable (worklog 2026-06-16): the MSVC500 toolchain ships retail MFC 4.2
(`C:\msvc\mfc\{include,lib}`); `<afx.h>` compiles, `nafxcw.lib` links (with the Win32
import libs), and the library code is **byte-identical** to the original
(`CObject::IsKindOf` matches opcode-for-opcode). MFC `CObject` always carries all 5
vtable slots (GetRuntimeClass / ~ / Serialize / AssertValid / Dump — `AssertValid`/`Dump`
are **not** `#ifdef _DEBUG`-guarded), so the layout matches the game's root.

Payoff (proxy over 50 MFC-named functions in `symbols.csv`): 7@100, 6 partial, 37 missing
→ ~43/50 would improve, plus the larger unnamed MFC surface.

## Why this is NOT a one-shot change

- `afx.h` is monolithic: it defines `CObject`/`CString`/`CPtrList`/`CArchive`/
  `CMapPtrToPtr`/… together, colliding with our 16 hand-rolled `C*` headers — they migrate
  as a unit, and `CObject` is the universal root.
- Signature divergence forces a wide sweep: MFC `GetRuntimeClass() const` vs ours
  (non-const) means **~120 override sites across 128 files** must gain `const`; MFC
  `Serialize(CArchive&)` vs ours (`CArchive*`); MFC `AssertValid()`/`Dump(CDumpContext&)`
  vs our `AssertValidOrSlot0c()`/`DumpOrSlot10(int)`.
- `// LIBRARY:` annotations cannot coexist with `// FUNCTION:` for the same address —
  otherwise the marker-hygiene gate fails. Replace `FUNCTION` with `LIBRARY` when
  reclaiming a symbol from `nafxcw.lib`.

So there is **no green checkpoint for a single blind pass**. Execute as staged increments,
each ending green (`just build` + `just gates` + targeted `just compare`).

## Tooling ready

- `tools/mfc/gen_library_annotations.py` → can bulk-emit `include/game/library_mfc.h`
  (`// LIBRARY: IMPERIALISM 0xADDR` + qualified name, inside `#if 0`). Prefer placing
  markers in the owning `.cpp` (e.g. `src/game/CObject.cpp`) so ownership stays obvious;
  use the generator for large batch stages (CString, collections) where a single header
  is cleaner. Second line must be the **true MFC name** (fix provisional names like
  `TNetMgr::GetCObjectRuntimeClass`→`CObject::GetRuntimeClass` in `symbols.csv` during
  the relevant stage).
- CMake `-DIMPERIALISM_LINK_MFC=ON` links `nafxcw.lib` + import libs (ON in `justfile`
  since stage 2). Import set now includes `oledlg.lib` (pulled in by `oledlgs2.obj`).
  `/FORCE:MULTIPLE` removed once duplicate hand-rolled bodies were replaced with
  `// LIBRARY:` markers (CString ctor/dtor, CArchive Close/FillBuffer, CMapPtrToPtr,
  CPtrList core, CDC/CClientDC/CGdiObject dtors, CDocument::DisconnectViews).

### LIBRARY marker shape (in-source)

When a function body is removed because `nafxcw.lib` owns the implementation, leave
comment-only ownership in the class `.cpp` — no empty stub body:

```cpp
// LIBRARY: IMPERIALISM 0x00412bf0
// CObject::AssertValid
```

reccmp pairs by address + qualified name; the marker is scanned from comments even when
wrapped in `#if 0` (see `library_msvc.h`), but in-source placement keeps
`function_ownership.csv` sync obvious.

## Progress (2026-06-16)

| Stage | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| 1 — signature prep | **done** | `Serialize(CArchive&)`, `AssertValid() const`, `Dump(CDumpContext&) const`; `CDumpContext` placeholder; `symbols.csv` renamed AssertValid/Dump |
| 2 — link MFC + CObject swap | **mostly done** | `IMPERIALISM_LINK_MFC=ON`; `LIBRARY` markers for CObject/CRuntimeClass core + duplicate CString/CArchive/CMapPtrToPtr/CPtrList/CDC/CDocument symbols; clean link (no `/FORCE:MULTIPLE`); `CRuntimeClass::Store` still local |
| 3 — CString | **done** | All `CString.cpp` bodies reclaimed as `// LIBRARY:`; header uses MFC names (`operator=`, `operator+=`, `AllocBuffer`, `ConcatCopy`, `GetBuffer`, …); manual callers updated; `CompareAnsiStringsWithMbcsAwareness` stays local |
| 4 — CPtrList/CPtrArray/CObList | partial | CPtrList ctor/dtor/RemoveAll/RemoveHead/RemoveTail/GetRuntimeClass reclaimed; node helpers still local |
| 5 — CArchive/CMapPtrToPtr | partial | Close/FillBuffer + `WriteObject` `Serialize(*this)` reclaimed; buffer R/W bodies still local |
| 6 — CWnd/CDC/… GUI | pending | needs `CWinApp`/`AfxWinInit` scaffolding |

Open items for stage 2:

- `classCObject` global (`0x006706e0`) — was a `// GLOBAL:` in our `CObject.cpp`; now
  supplied by MFC data. Confirm reccmp global pairing after a `just compare` pass.
- Scalar deleting destructor (`0x00415f00`) — stays `// SYNTHETIC:` (compiler-generated).
- Pull in `<afx.h>` / drop hand-rolled `CObject.h` once duplicate-symbol pressure from
  overlapping CString/CArchive modules is manageable (or staged with `/FORCE:MULTIPLE`).

## Suggested stage order

1. **Prep sweep (green, no MFC yet):** make our `CObject` virtuals match MFC signatures
   — `GetRuntimeClass() const`, `Serialize(CArchive&)`, rename slots 3/4 to
   `AssertValid() const` / `Dump(CDumpContext&) const`. Sweep all ~120 overrides. Build
   green. **Done.**
2. **Link MFC + core swap:** turn on `IMPERIALISM_LINK_MFC`; remove local `CObject`/
   `CRuntimeClass` bodies reclaimed by `nafxcw.lib`; add `// LIBRARY:` markers in the
   owning `.cpp`; resolve link order; build + reccmp. **In progress.**
3. **CString**, then **CPtrList/CPtrArray/CObList**, then **CArchive/CMapPtrToPtr**, each
   as its own green increment with `LIBRARY` markers (in-source or `library_mfc.h`) and a
   `just compare` delta.
4. **CWnd/CDC/CGdiObject/CDialog/CDocument/CView** GUI surface last (largest, needs the
   `CWinApp`/`AfxWinInit` app scaffolding for a clean static-MFC link).

Track the reccmp delta per stage; the proxy predicts the win concentrates in stages 3–5
(CString/collection/archive internals are the bulk of the unmatched MFC surface).
acceptance_criteria: Next MFC migration stage replaces hand-rolled bodies with real MFC declarations/LIBRARY markers, links cleanly, and passes targeted compare plus gates.

notes:
Progress note 2026-07-02 (verification only, no risky edits this pass): checked
the "Still TBD" list against current source state.

TCommandHandler (0x486650) is actually ALREADY DONE -- `just compare 0x486650`
reports 100% match. The current body:
    void TCommandHandler::ConstructTCommandHandlerBaseState(TCommand* command) {
      command->OrphanRetStub_00487a00();
      command->Free();
    }
is real (not a stub, not a fake bridge) and correct. It's a genuine
architectural finding that the NAME is wrong though: the disassembly shows
`this` (ECX) is never read inside the body at all -- it only calls two
virtuals on the `command` PARAMETER (slots 0x2c and 0x1c on TCommand, the
latter being TObject::Free) and returns. This is not construction behavior
in any sense; slot 0x25 is misnamed "ConstructTCommandHandlerBaseState" by
Ghidra's default heuristic for this class specifically. Left the name as-is
per Hard Rule 6 (rename only when necessary, and a vtable-slot rename needs
coordinating every override across the hierarchy -- not worth the risk for a
cosmetic-only fix, especially given this exact ticket's own revert history
warning about vtable-sensitive edits). Noting it here so nobody re-investigates
"why is TCommandHandler still a Construct*BaseState stub" -- it isn't a stub.

Remaining 5 items in the "Still TBD" table are confirmed still genuine empty
stubs (`return 0;`, unowned real logic) as of this check: TSuperArmyRoster
(0x4aa540), TPopGrowthOrder (0x4b8160), TDeluxeText (0x5b62a0), TDealTabControl
(0x5bc780), TNavyHumanPlayer (0x59efc0) -- all still `// FUNCTION:` marked but
with placeholder `return 0;` bodies. Did NOT attempt these this pass: the
ticket's own history records a prior revert on exactly TDealTabControl/
TDeluxeText/TPopGrowthOrder because wrong virtual signatures scrambled vtables
-- that's real, session-ending-risk territory (vtable corruption can cascade
across many unrelated classes) and deserves a dedicated, careful session with
the `vtable-matching` skill rather than being folded into a broader sweep.
TSuperArmyRoster is separately flagged "Large; needs TPageView field recovery"
-- also not a quick win.

Recommend: whoever picks this up next should tackle ONE of the five at a time,
with `just vtable <Class>` clean before AND after each attempt, and be ready
to fully revert (not partially patch) if a vtable regresses -- per this
ticket's own prior lesson.

design:
# MFC Collection/List Recovery Plan

This tracks the list-family inconsistencies found while replacing the old
`ApplicationUiRootEmbeddedList` scaffold with `TApplication::trackedEntries`
(`CList<void*, void*>`). The common failure mode is trusting Ghidra-adjacent names
or vtable overreads instead of constructor writes, RTTI chains, and MFC collection
layout evidence.

## Current Findings

| ID | Surface | Evidence | Status | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | `TApplication::trackedEntries` embedded vtable `0x00648ca8` | Vtable slot 0 inherits `CObject::GetRuntimeClass`; no derived `CRuntimeClass`; ctor writes subobject vptr at `TApplication + 0x2c`; public `CList<void*, void*>` API matches the insert/remove body. | Fixed | Source is `CList<void*, void*>`; stale symbol rows now use `TApplication::trackedEntries` instead of fake standalone `EmbeddedList` identity. |
| L2 | MFC array vtable `0x00672eac` | `config/symbols.csv` labeled it `TIndexAndRankList::'vftable'`, but `TIndexAndRankList` source/manifest vtable is `0x00659c58`; `0x00672eac` sits next to `CPtrArray::classRuntimeClass` and the retail MFC array functions. | Fixed | Global symbol renamed to `CPtrArray::'vftable'`; it is no longer used as the game `TIndexAndRankList` identity in `symbols.csv`. |
| L3 | `TIndexAndRankList` manifest ancestry | Header says `TIndexAndRankList : CPtrArray`; `config/classes/TIndexAndRankList.yml` says `base: TSortedPtrList`. | Won't-fix (manifest) | Ground truth: ctor (via 0x00488400 family) writes a CPtrArray-derived (size 0x18) vtable; header `TIndexAndRankList : CPtrArray` is the source of truth. The `config/classes/*.yml` manifests are generated reference only and are not reconciled — source headers win. |
| L4 | `TSortedPtrList` / `TPtrList` vtable crossing | Two distinct Family-1 (CPtrArray, size 0x18) classes: vtable `0x00649010` and `0x00649068`. | Fixed | Ground truth from ctor vtable writes + RTTI: `0x00488400` writes `0x00649068` (GetRuntimeClass `0x00488510` → RTTI `0x00648eb0`); the sibling `0x00649010` has dtor `0x00488390`, GetRuntimeClass `0x004883e0` → RTTI `0x00648e98`. `symbols.csv` had named BOTH scalar dtors (`0x00488390`, `0x004884c0`) `TSortedPtrList`, mispairing our `~` to `0x00488390`. De-duplicated `0x00488390` → `TSortedPtrListSibling_649010`; source class (VTABLE `0x00649068`) now matches 100%. |
| L5 | `TList` / `TSortedList` base edge + missing base slots | `TList`/`TSortedList` are siblings; their shared in-construction base vtable is `0x006485c0`. Source base `TPtrList` was missing virtual slots `0x64-0x78`. | Fixed | Ctors `0x00487a90`/`0x00487e50` both write base vtable `0x006485c0` then their own (`0x00648ee0`/`0x00648f78`) — siblings, no `TList`↔`TSortedList` edge. Added the 6 missing base virtuals (`VirtualSlot64..78`) to `TPtrList`; this fixed derived `TArmyStackList`/`TTaskList` vtables (their new/override virtuals had been landing in the wrong slot). |
| L6 | `ProvinceCollectionVirtualShape` local facade | `TCivDescription.cpp` declared a local virtual shape. | Fixed | Facade no longer present in source. |
| L7 | `CIterator` raw node cursor | `CIterator` reads the embedded `CPtrList` head from `TPtrList + 8`. | Accepted | Kept as a deliberate cursor (`include/game/CIterator.h`); needed for compare. |

## Fix Order

1. **Symbol identity cleanup:** fix stale `symbols.csv` rows for L1/L2. This is low
   risk and prevents future audits from rediscovering fake class identities.
2. **Manifest source cleanup:** repair the list-family base/vtable facts in
   `config/classes/*.yml` or the Ghidra labels feeding them, then run the class
   generator only for the affected list classes.
3. **Source model cleanup:** after manifests agree with headers, replace local
   list facades such as `ProvinceCollectionVirtualShape`.
4. **Codegen cleanup:** only after the class model is stable, revisit raw node
   cursor code (`CIterator`) and compare public API alternatives.

## Evidence Commands

Use the wrappers where possible; run Ghidra commands serially because the project
lock is exclusive.

```sh
just ghidra-vtable-dump TApplicationTrackedEntries 0x00648ca8
just ghidra-vtable-dump CPtrArray 0x00672eac
just ghidra-vtable-dump TIndexAndRankList 0x00659c58
just ghidra-vtable-dump TSortedPtrList 0x00649068
just ghidra-listing 0x00488400 0x00488530
just ghidra-listing 0x00534870 0x005348f0
```

Acceptance for each fix is `just build` plus the relevant narrow gate
(`just synthetic-gate`, `just vtable-collision-gate`, or `just manifest-gate`
when touching class manifests). Full `just gates` is currently known to fail on
broad generated-decls drift unrelated to this list audit.
acceptance_criteria: List-family manifests/symbols no longer reintroduce fake identities; any remaining CIterator/raw cursor work is evidence-backed and build/gates pass for touched surfaces.

title: Trace startup-loop map/turn-node advancement
description: From docs/reference/startup-loop-view-refresh.md. Runtime path can look idle because first message-cycle rebuild reason is not Wpam/Wnrt. Next advancement work should trace TSimMgr map/turn nodes and follow-up turn-event handlers that populate them. Trace targets include FindNodeByTagOrBuildIfMissing paths for Wpam/Wnrt, turn-event handlers, and view refresh gates.
design:
# Startup Loop View Refresh Findings

## Observed runtime path

`just debug-timeout` with breakpoints on startup and turn-event methods shows the
message loop is not dead. Startup reaches this chain:

```text
WinMain
  -> ImperialismApp::InitInstance
  -> CWinThread::Run / CWinApp::Run
  -> CMainFrame::OnStartupCommand100
  -> ImperialismApp::HandleStartupCommand100
  -> TSimMgr::AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine
  -> TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C(0, 0)
```

At `TSimMgr::AdvanceGlobalTurnStateMachine`, the live object state was:

| Field | Offset | Value |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `turnStateCode` | `+0x00` | `1` |
| `mode` | `+0x04` | `1` |
| `quarterGateTick2c` | `+0x2c` | `0` |
| `field30` | `+0x30` | `7` |
| `redrawEnabled` | `+0x40` | `0` |

The state machine case for code `1` advances `turnStateCode` to `3` and dispatches
`g_pUiRuntimeContext->DispatchTurnEventSlot4C(0, 0)`. It does not post a second
startup command on this path.

## Why the loop looked idle

`TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C(0, 0)` takes the code-0 full-refresh path:

```text
mainView->CallVoidSlotA0()
CWMgrIterator::FirstWindow()
while (iter.More()) {
  if (node->controlTag == 'Wpam' || node->controlTag == 'Wnrt')
    node->RebuildWindowContentSlot1D0()
}
```

The debugger shows `CWMgrIterator::FirstWindow()` returns `0`, so
`g_LiveViewRegistry` is empty. The message loop is still running; the first
refresh sweep has no registered windows to rebuild, then the app waits for more
messages.

After recovering the `TWindow` construction path, the same breakpoint sequence now
returns a live registry node:

| Probe | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `CWMgrIterator::FirstWindow()` return | `0x1521118` |
| first node vtable | `0x0049d958` |
| first node `controlTag` | `0x57494e44` (`'WIND'`) |

The code-0 refresh path is therefore no longer empty. The first registered node is
not one of the two rebuild tags (`'Wpam'` / `'Wnrt'`), so the next advancement work
is to recover the concrete window/dialog factory path that creates those tagged
nodes and the follow-up turn-event handlers that populate them.

### `'Wpam'` / `'Wnrt'` tag provenance (2026-06)

Static search shows **no** C++ assignment of `0x6d617057` / `0x74726e57` in manual
source or autogen exports. The tags are four-character UI control names embedded in
turn-event dialog resources; they appear on child nodes when
`TView::InitializeUiResourceEntryFrameAndParent` / `RegisterUiResourceEntry` parses
a template during a turn-event factory callback.

Known wired factory today: `BuildTurnOrderNavigationWindow` in
`turn_event_dialog_factory.cpp` sets `kControlTagWind` (`'WIND'`) on `TGameWindow`
instances — matching the live registry node seen at startup. Map-panel tags
(`'Wpam'` / `'Wnrt'`) are expected from **unported** factories in the same registry
(`BuildTurnEventDialogResourcesForEvent547Or7D8`, `BuildTurnEventDialogUiByCode`, and
`TIncludeView::BuildTurnEventFactoryPacket`) once turn codes `0x7d8`–`0x7de` run
through the cross-code path.

Next trace targets:

1. Port `TIncludeView::BuildTurnEventFactoryPacket` (`0x48cf10`) — builds the `'Incl'`
   packet and invokes registered factories by event code.
2. Port `BuildTurnEventDialogResourcesForEvent547Or7D8` (`0x4295a0`) — likely creates
   strategic-map panel controls for diplomacy/map turn events.
3. Confirm rebuilt nodes are `TWindow`-lineage (slot byte `0x1d0` =
   `TWindow::OrphanCallChain_C2_I10_0048e120`) via vtable dump on first `'Wpam'`
   registry hit after a non-zero turn event.

## Source-model evidence

The source used to be asymmetric:

| Class | Constructor behavior | Destructor behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TWindow` | `TWindow::TWindow() : TView() {}` | removes `this` from `g_LiveViewRegistry` |
| `TFloatWindow` | calls `TWindow()`, then `g_LiveViewRegistry.AddTail(this)` | inherits the `TWindow` unlink path |

Original evidence for `0x0048d500` shows the real `TWindow` construction body is
not empty. It builds the `TView` base, constructs the embedded `TDialogBehavior`
region at `+0x74`, links `this` into the live-view registry, initializes the gold
color descriptor, and writes self pointers into the `+0x64` / dialog-behavior
owner fields.

The current source now models that direction directly:

- `TWindow` owns a real `TDialogBehavior` member at `+0x74`.
- `TWindow::TWindow` inserts `this` into `g_LiveViewRegistry` with `CPtrList::AddHead`.
- `TFloatWindow::TFloatWindow` no longer re-adds itself to the registry; the derived
  constructor relies on the base constructor, matching the original sequence.

## Advancement plan

1. Continue replacing generic turn-event stubs with real `TViewMgr` / `TMacViewMgr`
   methods.
   - Start with the dispatch methods reached from `DispatchTurnEventSlot4C`:
     `0x005d6bf0`, `0x005d6c10`, `0x005d6c30`, `0x005d6cd0`..`0x005d71b0`,
     and `0x005d7c40` onward.
   - Keep virtual dispatch as real methods on `TViewMgr`, `TMacViewMgr`, or the
     recovered dialog/view class. Avoid raw `vftable[]` indexing and call-convention
     casts for recoverable class methods.
2. Improve the strategic-map side effects needed by turn-event handlers.
   - Prioritize `TMacViewMgr` slots that refresh map/city panels:
     `0x0050d310`, `0x0050d360`, `0x0050d470`, `0x0050d5b0`, `0x0050d920`, and
     `0x0050d950`.
   - Replace wrapper names with semantic real methods once the receiver and slot
     are verified from the listing.
3. Recover the concrete registered window/dialog classes that should appear in the
   code-0 sweep with tags `'Wpam'` and `'Wnrt'`.
   - Use constructor/vtable evidence, not only `controlTag`, to name the classes.
   - Once the classes are known, replace the local `UiWindowTraversalNode` vtable-view
     with real virtuals on the recovered owner.
4. Validate each slice with:
   - `just sync-ownership && just regen-stubs && just build` after marker moves.
   - `just compare <addresses>` for changed functions.
   - `just debug-timeout` breakpoints on `CWMgrIterator::FirstWindow`,
     `TViewMgr::DispatchTurnEventSlot4C`, and selected `TMacViewMgr` slots to prove
     the loop advances past the current empty-refresh point.
