title: Represent MSVC5 per-TU template twin copies in reccmp
description: From docs/TODO.md and FABLE_SUGGESTIONS.md. Per-TU original copies of CList/CArray/header-inline functions cannot pair against one recomp COMDAT today, e.g. WNetMgr copies 0x5e4540..0x5e4a60 and IncludeView copies 0x479a80/0x479b00. Extend vendored reccmp with a twin/alias annotation or equivalent so additional original addresses can score against the same recomp symbol.
design:
# Structural problems & proposed fixes (Fable, 2026-07-01)

Big-picture issues identified while porting the UI foundation classes, in impact
order. Each entry: the problem, the evidence, the proposed fix, expected payoff.

## 1. Header-inline ctors/dtors — a systemic match ceiling

**Problem.** The original source defined the T-hierarchy's constructors and
destructors *inside the class bodies in headers* (implicitly `inline`). MSVC500
therefore inlines them into `CreateObject`, into derived dtor chains, and at
`new T()` callsites. Our reconstruction defines them out-of-line in `.cpp`, so
the same sites compile to a `call` instead of inlined code.

**Evidence.**
- `TIncludeView::CreateObject` (0x48cc40), `TWindow::CreateObject` (0x48d090),
  `TControl::CreateObject` (0x48e430) all contain their class's ctor fully
  inlined (registry `AddHead` CPlex code and all); our macro-generated
  `CreateObject` calls the out-of-line ctor → pairs at ~36%.
- `TIncludeView::~TIncludeView` (0x48ce70) contains `~TView` fully inlined
  (vptr rewrite to 0x649858, child-list delete, +0x58 CString dtor); ours would
  emit `call TView::~TView`.

**Fix.** One careful experiment on TView: move `TView::~TView` (and later the
ctor) into `TView.h` as a class-body definition, then force the out-of-line copy
that the `// FUNCTION: 0x0048a9d0` marker needs (candidates: keep one TU where
inlining fails naturally via the scalar-deleting-dtor SYNTHETIC, or check MSVC5's
behavior for address-taken/virtual-dtor emission). Verify 0x48a9d0 still pairs,
then measure 0x48ce70/0x48cc40-style scores. If it works, roll out
hierarchy-wide.

**Payoff.** Hundreds of ctor/dtor-adjacent functions across ~400 classes are
currently capped at ~36–70% by this one modeling decision.

## 2. MSVC5 per-TU twins — a reccmp expressiveness gap

**Problem.** A header-inline function gets a fresh out-of-line copy in every
translation unit that needs one, and the 1997 linker performed no identical-code
folding — so the exe contains N byte-identical copies at N addresses. Our source
defines the function once; reccmp pairs strictly one orig address to one recomp
symbol, so N−1 copies are permanently counted "unported" and accrete junk names.

**Evidence.** `TView::~TView`: 0x48a9d0 (paired) plus byte-identical twins
0x48cb00, 0x48ec30, 0x48ee00 (verified instruction-for-instruction); TView's
scalar deleting destructor twin at 0x48cad0. These carried fictional curated
names ("TScroller::CreateTScrollerInstance", "TButton::CreateTButtonInstance")
that misdirected multiple sessions.

**Fix.** Extend the vendored reccmp fork with a twin/alias annotation (e.g.
`// TWIN: IMPERIALISM 0xADDR` following a `// FUNCTION:`-owned definition, or a
multi-address marker) that pairs additional original addresses against the same
recomp symbol and scores each independently.

**Payoff.** Converts a whole category of fake-unported functions into measured
coverage; removes a standing source of misleading names. The four TView twins
are the tip — every header-inline function in a 400-class hierarchy potentially
has copies.

## 3. Exploit the RTTI oracle fully (Mac evidence is second-class)

**Problem.** The binary's MFC `CRuntimeClass` descriptors are intact,
compiler-emitted ground truth — true class name, **object size**, base-class
edge, `CreateObject` address — and until now nothing checked our curated data
against them. Meanwhile inheritance/layout work has leaned on the Mac
CodeWarrior dump, which is a *different build for a different platform*:
useful as a name/signature hint, second-class as evidence. The Windows RTTI
supersedes it wherever both speak.

**Done already** (commit aaea549d): `just rtti-oracle` +
`config/rtti_class_oracle.csv` (471 descriptors, 403 game classes); 326 wrong
symbols.csv names fixed; 307 `CreateObject` SYNTHETIC claims applied.

**Remaining fixes.**
- **Size gate:** cross-check every modeled class (`sizeof` via ASSERT_SIZE or a
  compile-time probe) against the oracle's `object_size`; report mismatches.
  Catches layout errors mechanically instead of via crash archaeology.
- **Base-edge import:** the `m_pBaseClass` chain gives the entire
  single-inheritance tree; diff it against our modeled `class X : public Y`
  edges and against `IMPLEMENT_DYNCREATE(X, Y)` second arguments.
- **GetRuntimeClass claims:** each descriptor's class has a trivial
  `MOV EAX, <descriptor>; RET` slot-0 override (e.g. 0x48cb90 → TScroller's
  0x6495b8); these are macro-generated and mass-claimable the same way
  CreateObject was.

## 4. Ghidra database code gaps distort scores and searches

**Problem.** Chunks of real code are undefined in the Ghidra DB (no function, no
instructions): switch bodies behind jump tables, functions reached only via
vtables/thunks. Consequences: xrefs and decompiles come back empty, and reccmp
cannot disassemble the *original* side past an indirect `jmp`, so byte-equivalent
ports score absurdly low.

**Evidence.** `CMcWindow::OnWindowStateMsg468` (0x493800) scored 26% while being
byte-identical. RESOLVED 2026-07-02: not a reccmp-disassembler issue — Ghidra had
defined the switch's *case bodies* as standalone functions (junk symbols.csv rows at
0x493819/29/39 + a paired autogen stub), which clamped reccmp's max_size window to
0x19 bytes. Deleting the rows + regen-stubs took it to 98%. reccmp's InstructGen
handles in-function jump tables correctly (verified standalone). The general fix for
this class of junk (case-body pseudo-functions in the Ghidra DB) belongs to the
gap-repair pass below. 0x5742b0 and several CMcWindow handlers were invisible to
`ghidra-listing`/xrefs until raw-disasm'd.

**Fix.** A gap-scan pass: walk `int3`-padded boundaries, vtable slot targets,
ILT jmp targets, and message-map `pfn`s; `createFunction` each undefined target
in the Ghidra DB; re-export the project archive. Optionally teach the reccmp
fork to follow jump tables on the original side.

## 5. Tooling odds and ends

- **Batch compare:** RESOLVED — `just compare 0xA 0xB 0xC` and
  `just compare --file src/game/X.cpp` run one `reccmp --json` parse.
- **`gen-class` is dead code:** still open. It requires `config/classes/<Class>.yml`
  manifests and `config/classes/` does not exist (the manifest system is dormant —
  see the note in `tools/common/class_manifest.py`). Either seed manifests from the
  RTTI oracle (name, size, base are all known now) or retire the tool. The dormancy
  also cost `gen-recovered-fields-from-headers` its per-class base offsets
  (TGreatPower pilot rows had to be dropped from the golden test, 2026-07-02).
- **`sync-ownership` is add-only:** RESOLVED — deletion-reconciling for
  `marker_sync` rows (curated notes never pruned), and `just regen-stubs` now runs
  it (plus `symbols-integrity-gate`) automatically.
- **symbols.csv fragility:** RESOLVED — `symbols-integrity-gate` (in `just gates`,
  before every `regen-stubs`, and at the end of `sync-ghidra`) rejects a misplaced
  header/duplicate addresses; the resync merge drops rows colliding with
  `// VTABLE:` addresses instead of re-introducing them (2026-07-02 overhaul).
- **Curated-name provenance:** RESOLVED — symbols.csv carries a trailing
  `provenance` column (rtti/mac/manual/ghidra-auto), preserved by the merge.
acceptance_criteria: A tested annotation/mechanism pairs known twin copies without fake source bodies, and at least one documented twin family is covered.
close_reason: Acceptance met: the // TEMPLATE: annotation is the mechanism representing MSVC5 per-TU template twin copies in reccmp — supported end-to-end by reccmp's parser/marker.py plus the repo's sync_function_ownership.py/function_ownership.py (covered by the tooling test suite), and now in production use (7 TEMPLATE markers across global_data_tables.cpp, TModuleLibraryCacheTableStateB.cpp, TTurnEventDialogFactoryRegistry.cpp). It pairs known twin copies WITHOUT fake source bodies: e.g. 0x49b270 CMap<void*,void*,CacheRecord*,CacheRecord*>::~CMap pairs at 97.92%. Documented twin families covered: the CMap m_tableA/m_tableB twins (0x49ae30/0x49b270) of TModuleLibraryCacheTableStateB, plus the WNet CList<void*,void*>/CArray<void*,void*> twins (0x5e4540/0x5e4580/0x5e4780/0x5e47b0). Mechanism adopted+validated during bd 1uj.44.

title: Reconcile TDefendProvinceMission city score record typing
description: From docs/TODO.md networking/orphan follow-ups. TDefendProvinceMission has raw cityScoreTable byte-offset casts at lines around 73/129/306/390 into TGlobalMapCityScoreRecord, including float read at +0x9c where the record declares int cityScoreValue. Reconcile dual int/float use and replace byte offsets with typed fields.
acceptance_criteria: TGlobalMapCityScoreRecord represents the observed int/float use honestly; raw byte offsets in TDefendProvinceMission are removed where evidence supports it.
notes:
Investigation 2026-07-02 (root cause found, fix NOT applied -- this touches a
widely-used struct offset and needs more certainty first; see below):

Confirmed the int/float bug is real and precisely diagnosed. TDefendProvinceMission
::ResetValue0CToZero (0x53ed00, "ComputeDefendProvinceMissionTerrainAdjacencyScoreFromTile14"
per Ghidra) contains:
    FILD dword ptr [ECX + EAX*0x8 + 0x9c]
FILD is the x86 INTEGER load-and-convert-to-float instruction, NOT a raw float
bit-reinterpretation. This proves the original reads TGlobalMapCityScoreRecord
::cityScoreValue (an `int` per the struct, confirmed by 4 independent
consumers: TAttackProvinceMission.cpp x2 via static_cast<float>(...cityScoreValue),
TGreatPower.cpp returning it directly, TMultiplayerMgr.cpp packing it into a
network packet as `int cityScoreValue9C`) and does a genuine int->float VALUE
conversion. TDefendProvinceMission.cpp's current
`*reinterpret_cast<float*>(cityScoreTable + 0x9c + tileIndex*0xa8)` is wrong:
it bit-reinterprets instead of converting, and will read garbage since
cityScoreValue's actual int bit pattern is not a valid float representation
of the same number.

BUT: found while tracing this that the receiver for the FILD is NOT
g_pGlobalMapState->cityScoreTable's own address computation -- it's
`[g_pGlobalMapState + 0x10]`, not `[g_pGlobalMapState + 0x0c]` where
TMapMgr.h currently declares cityScoreTable. Raw disasm:
    MOV ECX,[0x006a43d4]      ; ECX = g_pGlobalMapState
    MOV ECX,[ECX + 0x10]      ; ECX = *(g_pGlobalMapState + 0x10)
    ... EAX = tileIndex * 0x15 (then *8 via addressing mode = *0xa8) ...
    FILD dword ptr [ECX + EAX*8 + 0x9c]
Stride (0xa8) and sub-offset (0x9c) both match TGlobalMapCityScoreRecord
exactly -- this IS cityScoreTable, just read through +0x10 instead of the
header's declared +0x0c. Same +0x10 pattern independently found while
investigating bd 1uj.8 (TileHasMovementClassId/
ComputeAggregateWeightedChildCostForMatchingType5NavyOrders also read
`[g_pGlobalMapState+0x10]` with the identical 0xa8 stride).

Two functions now independently point at the same conclusion: TMapMgr's real
cityScoreTable pointer sits at +0x10, not the header's declared +0x0c -- i.e.
there's an undocumented 4-byte field between terrainStateTable (+0x08,
independently well-evidenced elsewhere) and the true cityScoreTable slot.
NOT fixed here because:
  1. g_pGlobalMapState->cityScoreTable (the named field, at the header's
     current +0x0c) is used in DOZENS of already-built, gates-passing files.
     If the header's +0x0c is genuinely wrong, shifting it to +0x10 would
     silently change what every one of those call sites reads -- high blast
     radius for a change I can't fully verify without checking whether those
     call sites are ALSO currently scoring poorly (I did not have time to
     spot-check this with `just compare`).
  2. Don't yet know what the missing/misplaced field at +0x0c actually is,
     so I can't write a correct declaration for it (just leaving a 4-byte
     pad would be a guess, which the project's evidence-required rule
     disallows).

Recommended next steps: (1) spot-check `just compare` on a heavy
cityScoreTable consumer (e.g. TGreatPower.cpp:172's function) to see if it's
ALREADY scoring poorly -- if so, that's independent confirmation the header
offset is wrong project-wide, not just in these two callers; (2) find what's
really at TMapMgr+0x0c (check ctor/ReadFrom/WriteTo for a 4-byte write there
that's currently unaccounted for); (3) once resolved, fix TMapMgr.h's field
order/offsets (same style as bd 1uj.4's TSimMgr fix) and retype
TDefendProvinceMission.cpp's raw reinterpret_cast<float*> read into a real
`static_cast<float>(record.cityScoreValue)`. This will also very likely
resolve/simplify bd 1uj.8's TileHasMovementClassId/
ComputeAggregateWeightedChildCostForMatchingType5NavyOrders receiver work
(both hit the same +0x10 field).

Pausing here -- root cause is well-evidenced but the blast radius of the
actual fix needs more verification before committing to it.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed: TMapMgr.h had terrainStateTable/cityScoreTable/tileOwnershipTable/cityScoreTotal all declared 4 bytes too early (a missing 4-byte-scalar-field gap between the TObject head and terrainStateTable). Ground truth from TMapMgr::ReadFrom's decompile (0x50e620, Ghidra's own field_0xNN offsets): field_0xc is the terrainStateTable pointer (0x1950*0x24-byte buffer), field_0x10 is cityScoreTable (0x180*0xa8 stride), matching the struct exactly. Triple-confirmed by raw disassembly of TDefendProvinceMission::ResetValue0CToZero (0x53ed00) and TGreatPower::ComputeAdvisoryMapNodeScoreFactorByCaseMetric (0x4e8750), both using FILD (int-to-float conversion, not bit-reinterpret) on cityScoreValue at the record's +0x9c, and by 3 pre-existing raw-offset casts elsewhere (TCouncilTickerAnimation.cpp, TMinor.cpp, TWorldView.cpp) that were already using the correct ground-truth offsets, bypassing the buggy header. Shifted terrainStateTable/cityScoreTable/tileOwnershipTable/cityScoreTotal to their correct offsets (+0xc/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18) and added 4 new placeholder fields for the previously-missing +0x04..+0x0c gap. Fixed TDefendProvinceMission::ResetValue0CToZero's actual bug: replaced the raw reinterpret_cast<float*> bit-reinterpretation with a proper static_cast<float>(cityRecord.cityScoreValue) conversion, matching the confirmed FILD semantics. Build+gates+format-check pass; stats: +3 aligned functions, 20 improved, only 2 small (<4pp) regressions from codegen reshuffling in an otherwise-correct fix.

title: Port TMultiplayerMgr emitters and handlers
description: From docs/TODO.md networking follow-ups. Unported 0x540xxx-0x54c TMultiplayerMgr-TU emitters/handlers include CreateAndSendTurnEvent11/12/1B/1C 0x5493c0/0x5494b0/0x5498d0/0x5499b0, DispatchTurnEventPacketWithCodeAndPayloadBuffer 0x549ad0, DispatchTileRedrawInvalidateEvent 0x54ab20, HandleDiplomacyTurnEventPacketByCode 0x543910, EnsureGameFlowStateAndPostTurnEvent5E5 0x544540, EmitTurnEvent10ForFlaggedNationSlots 0x544720, SetNationStatusAwolByNationIdAndDispatchNotices 0x54b930. All appear __thiscall on g_pGameFlowState; verify ECX per method. Also investigate TNetMgr method at 0x407f77 ILT target and TProxyGreatPower::AddToNationMetricAtField10 0x540a00 empty repo body.
acceptance_criteria: Selected emitters/handlers are ported as real methods with TNetMgr::Send callers preserved; ECX evidence recorded; targeted compare and gates pass.
notes:
Analysis started 2026-07-02 (no port committed — each emitter needs per-function investigation). Owner class = TMultiplayerMgr (g_pGameFlowState is TMultiplayerMgr*); the family follows the ported CreateAndSendTurnEvent13/20/21 pattern (TMultiplayerMgr.cpp:153/179/205): fill a 'struct XxxPacket : NetMessage' {eventCode+0, fromNetworkId+4, toNetworkId+8, messageLength+0xc}, then packetTag(0x74696d65)+0x10, activeNationId(byte, g_pLocalizationTable->GetActiveNationId())+0x14, event fields, then g_pNetMgr006a6014->Send(&packet, flag).

First emitter fully mapped from 0x5493c0 listing — CreateAndSendTurnEvent11_MapOffsetAndFlags, thiscall, 5 args RET 0x14: struct = {NetMessage; int packetTag@0x10; u8 activeNationId@0x14; u8 mapMode@0x18(arg1); int selector@0x1c(arg2); int mapCoord@0x20(arg3 - offset); short@0x24(arg4); short@0x26(arg5)}; eventCode=0x11, messageLength=0x28, toNetworkId=(g_pLocalizationTable->field44==1)?0:-1.

BLOCKER surfaced: the map-offset read is g_pGlobalMapState[+0xc] (arg2==0) / [+0x10] (arg2==1) used as an INT and subtracted from arg3, but TMapMgr models +0xc/+0x10 as pointer fields (terrainStateTable/cityScoreTable, well-evidenced from ReadFrom). Resolve whether 0x6a43d4's +0xc/+0x10 are dual-purpose int coords or whether a different object is meant, BEFORE porting (Hard Rule 12 — don't force a wrong model). Same investigation likely recurs across the other emitters (0x5494b0/0x5498d0/0x5499b0/0x549ad0/0x54ab20/0x543910/0x544540/0x544720/0x54b930). Remaining scope ~10 emitters + TNetMgr 0x407f77 + TProxyGreatPower::AddToNationMetricAtField10 0x540a00.

title: Locate DataHunkMessage and PhaseDataMessage on Windows
description: From docs/TODO.md networking follow-ups. Mac oracle has DataHunkMessage::{Create16, ReadData(void*) const, Release} and PhaseDataMessage::{CheckSync, SetSync}, used by TMultiplayerMgr::DoGameDataHunk / ReceiveStreamMessage. Windows locations still unknown; likely surface in receive path through TWNetSessionManager::TryReceiveNetworkPacketIntoResizableBuffer callers and WNetMgr GetMessage/HandleMessage analogues in 0x5e3xxx band. Ruled out: 0x487820 TCommand base ctor, 0x49e500 news TNewGameCommand; Mac TEventList also unlocated.
acceptance_criteria: Windows candidates are located or ruled out with evidence; no Mac evidence is used to assign Windows addresses without binary proof.
notes:
Follow-up 2026-07-02: traced the real receive-dispatch chain via xrefs (new
evidence, not previously mapped):

  TWNetSessionManager::TryReceiveNetworkPacketIntoResizableBuffer (ported)
    -> [not yet found: who calls this]
  PopNextTurnEventPacketOrProcessSpecialQueueRecords (0x5e3f30, unported) --
    pops a queued packet, handles a few low-level protocol codes (0x21/3/5/7,
    0x31/0x101) itself (ack/heartbeat-like), returns the rest unhandled.
    Only xref: ILT thunk 0x403305.
  <- called (via thunk 0x403305) by
  TMultiplayerMgr::RouteAndProcessDiplomacyTurnStateEventQueue (0x545730,
    unported, real thiscall on TMultiplayerMgr confirmed by Ghidra param
    typing) -- pops every packet, switches on eventCode (packet's first
    dword, matches NetMessage::eventCode @ +0x00). Codes {1,2,6,10,0xb,0xf,
    0x18,0x19,0x1a,0x2e,0x2f,0x30} get queued to a deferred list
    (this->field_0x6c chain) instead of processed immediately; code 0xc gets
    a SEPARATE deferred list (this->field_0x70 chain) gated by a flag
    (this->field_0x69). Everything else dispatches straight through
    ProcessDiplomacyTurnStateEventStateMachine then frees the buffer.
  -> dispatches to
  ProcessDiplomacyTurnStateEventStateMachine (0x545940, 11459 bytes,
    unported, currently MISATTRIBUTED to TPoseMessageDialog by Ghidra's
    auto-analysis -- it's actually a free function or TMultiplayerMgr method,
    not a TPoseMessageDialog method; needs its own re-attribution pass). This
    is the real per-eventCode switch (40+ cases, 1..0x30) -- checked case 0xc
    specifically since it got separate deferred-queue treatment in the
    caller (plausible PhaseDataMessage-CheckSync/SetSync candidate): it's
    actually a diplomatic message-PROPOSAL dialog builder (constructs a
    TPoseMessageDialog instance, matches Ghidra's misattribution root
    cause) -- RULED OUT for DataHunkMessage/PhaseDataMessage, this is a
    high-level diplomacy UI event, not a low-level sync/data-transfer
    message.

Conclusion: DataHunkMessage/PhaseDataMessage most likely live at a LOWER
layer than this diplomacy-event switch -- probably inside
PopNextTurnEventPacketOrProcessSpecialQueueRecords's own special-case
handling (codes 0x21/3/5/7/0x31/0x101, not yet individually traced) or in
whatever calls TryReceiveNetworkPacketIntoResizableBuffer (still unlocated).
Next step: trace TryReceiveNetworkPacketIntoResizableBuffer's callers via
xrefs_to (same recipe used here: `source .env && uv run python -m
tools.ghidra.xrefs_to 0xADDR`, note `just` targets need GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR
sourced manually when called outside a `just` recipe), and individually
decompile the 0x21/3/5/7/0x31/0x101 case bodies inside 0x5e3f30 -- one of
those is more likely to be the raw data-hunk/phase-sync layer than the
diplomacy dialog switch.

Ruled out (additive to existing list): case 0xc of
ProcessDiplomacyTurnStateEventStateMachine (0x545940) -- diplomatic message
dialog builder, not DataHunkMessage/PhaseDataMessage.

design:
# InitInstance / ExitInstance Port Plan (handoff)

Goal: finish the window-open path — port `ImperialismApp::InitInstance` (`0x00412dc0`) and
`ExitInstance` (`0x00413780`) to faithful, fake-free C++. Work **leaf-up**: every callee must
be a real, correctly-typed declaration before the body can compile cleanly (no
`reinterpret_cast` of `(void)` stubs, no raw vtable, no fake calling conventions).

## Already done (keep, build on)

## Globals: cached splash flag (`g_cachedShowSplashFlag` / `0x006a2018`)

**Type:** `BOOL` — a copy of `CCommandLineInfo::m_bShowSplash`, **not** a `char*`, not the
filename, and not `m_nShellCommand`. `CCommandLineInfo` derives from `CObject`, so cmdInfo
**+0x04** is `m_bShowSplash`; `m_nShellCommand` is later in the object.

**Writer:** `SetCachedShowSplashFlag` @ `0x0049cc40`, called from `InitInstance` @
`0x00412f81` **after** `ParseCommandLine` and **before** `ProcessShellCommand`:

```asm
; cmdInfo object on stack at [ESP+0x1c]
MOV EDX, dword ptr [ESP + 0x20]   ; cmdInfo + 4 == m_bShowSplash
PUSH EDX
CALL SetCachedShowSplashFlag      ; -> g_cachedShowSplashFlag
```

**Reader:** `WrapperFor_AllocateWithFallbackHandler_At0049cc60` @ `0x0049cc60` (backdrop
creator from `CMainFrame::OnCreate`): creates the loading window only when
`g_cachedShowSplashFlag != 0` **and** `DAT_006a2050 == NULL`.

**MFC `m_nShellCommand` values** (standard `CCommandLineInfo` enum): `FileNew` = 0,
`FileOpen` = 1, `FilePrint` = 2, `FilePrintPreview` = 3, `FilePageSetup` = 4, `FileDDE` = 5,
`FileNothing` = 6. InitInstance’s *separate* early guard compares other cmdInfo fields (empty
filename at `[ESP+0x50]`, and `[ESP+0x2c] == 5`) — those are not what gets cached here.

**Runtime (2026-06):** backdrop window confirmed visible under `just debug` with this model.

1. `just ghidra-listing 0xADDR` for real offsets/convention; `just ghidra-decompile 0xADDR` for shape.
2. Promote/own the marker in the right `src/game/<Class>.cpp`; for new free helpers pick the file by
   `config/function_ownership.csv` address neighbors.
3. `just sync-ownership && just regen-stubs && just build` whenever a marker/ownership changes.
4. `just compare 0xADDR --verbose`; aim for a faithful shape (30–70% is fine — don't chase 100%,
   don't add pragmas). `just gates`; `just stats` for blast radius.
5. Expect first-link MFC re-pairing wobble (note 18) when new nafxcw functions get linked — flat
   aggregate, refresh baseline; don't revert clean MFC calls to chase it.

## Traps specific to this work

- Ghidra mislabels `InitInstance` as `CMainFrame::OnEndPrintPreview` and `ExitInstance` as
  `CAmbitDocument::SetForeignMinisterReadyFlag14`. Ignore the names; pair by address.
- A free callee invoked with `ECX=this` is a `__thiscall` method on that receiver — model it on the
  receiver class (e.g. the two auto-resolution helpers are ImperialismApp methods), never a fake
  `__fastcall`/`reinterpret_cast`.
- Do **not** model leaf helpers as `__fastcall(void*, int dummyEdx)` — use real methods or `__cdecl`
  with explicit parameters.
- `CSingleDocTemplate`/`CCommandLineInfo`/`ParseCommandLine`/`ProcessShellCommand`/`AddDocTemplate`/
  `SetRegistryKey` are real MFC — call them; the 3 doc/view `CRuntimeClass`es are data globals to
  `extern`, not classes to model.

        alerts.append(
            ParserAlert(
                code=AlertCode.FUNCTION_OUT_OF_ORDER,
                path=result.path,
                line_number=fun.line_number,
                target=fun.module,
                detail=(
                    f"fix: uv run python -m tools.workflow.reorder_marked_functions {result.path}"
                ),
            )
        )

Verified against a synthetic out-of-order test file -- alert now prints
inline, e.g.:
    7 : error: [IMPERIALISM] function_out_of_order  fix: uv run python -m
        tools.workflow.reorder_marked_functions <path>
`just gates` still exits 0 afterward (no regression from the patch).

Upstream concern: reccmp is presumably used by other projects beyond this
one, so the hardcoded `uv run python -m tools.workflow.reorder_marked_
functions` command is specific to this repo's tooling layout and would be
wrong/misleading for a different downstream project. Options for the
upstream version:
  (a) make the hint text configurable per-project (e.g. via reccmp-project.yml,
      something like `decomplint.function_out_of_order_hint: "<command>"`),
      falling back to no hint (current upstream behavior) if unset;
  (b) keep the hint generic/tool-agnostic ("run a marker-order-fixing pass on
      this file") without naming a specific command;
  (c) don't upstream this one at all and instead teach THIS repo's `just
      decomplint`/`just gates` wrapper (justfile) to post-process reccmp's
      output and append the hint itself, which avoids needing an upstream
      change for something this repo-specific. Probably the pragmatic choice
      -- evaluate before attempting the reccmp-side patch.

Lower priority than the worktree-exclusion patch (imperialism-decomp-7hi) --
that one causes silent data corruption; this one is a pure UX nicety.

title: Fix TSimMgr field-offset comment drift
description: From docs/TODO.md. TSimMgr.h field comments drift by 4 from field_64 onward. preferenceValues is +0x44..+0x5f, field_64 sits at +0x60, pad68 at +0x64, etc. Verify against ctor listing and fix comment names only if evidence agrees.
acceptance_criteria: TSimMgr offset comments align with ctor evidence and no layout/codegen-affecting edits are introduced.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-02: the original close on this issue was WRONG. A parallel
agent (agent-2, merged in commit 49bb5b2e) independently investigated the
same layout drift and found the actual bug is different from what I
described above: it's a single missing 4-byte field after preferenceValues
(pad60, pushing field_64 to its ORIGINAL +0x64, unchanged), plus 3 spurious
padding fields between the scenarioSetupRows arrays that needed REMOVING
(they're contiguous, not gapped). My original fix incorrectly shifted
field_64/fieldd8/field112/pad113/stateFlag114 (and everything between) by
-4 -- I had verified the TOTAL size matched ASSERT_SIZE(0x118) but never
cross-checked the constructor's scenario-row scatter-copy anchor points
(0xda/0xe8/0xf6/0x104), which is unambiguous ground truth that contradicts
my shift. Verified this definitively via that ctor evidence before merging;
agent-2's names (all matching the ORIGINAL pre-fix names, e.g. field_64,
fieldd8, field112, stateFlag114) are correct.

Lesson recorded in memory: when fixing a struct-offset drift, don't stop at
"total size matches" -- cross-check against every independent anchor point
you have evidence for (here, the ctor's own scatter-copy destination
offsets), not just the struct's final ASSERT_SIZE. A total-size match can
hide a compensating error elsewhere in the struct.

Current TSimMgr.h (post-merge) is correct per this cross-check and passing
build+gates+stats. No further action needed on this specific issue, but
flagging the false-positive close for the record.
